No atmosphere to scatter light → sky appears black from space/moon. Stars visible even during day.

M = f_o/f_e where f_o = focal length of objective, f_e = eyepiece. Larger f_o = more magnification.

Equal masses in elastic collision exchange velocities. First stops, second moves with 4 m/s.

a_max = ω²A = 16×0.1 = 1.6 m/s². Occurs at extremes (x = ±A).

R = u²sin(2θ)/g = 400×sin90°/10 = 40 m. Maximum range at 45°.

p = mv = 2×5 = 10 kg·m/s. Same units as impulse (N·s).
Cost of electricity is measured in:
1 unit = 1 kWh = 3.6×10⁶ J. Energy, not power. Electricity bills in units consumed.
Maxwell's equations (1860s) predicted EM waves. Hertz (1887) experimentally verified them.

Speed of transverse wave on stretched string with tension T and linear density μ:
v = √(T/μ). Faster with more tension, slower with heavier string. Used in tuning string instruments.
Work done by 10 N force displacing body 5 m at 60° to displacement:
W = Fd cos θ = 10×5×cos 60° = 10×5×0.5 = 25 J. Only component along displacement does work.
EMF of cell is measured by:
Potentiometer: null method, no current through cell, gives true EMF. Voltmeter draws small current.

P = P₁ + P₂ = 2 + (−1) = +1 D. Focal length = 1 m (convex).
Inductive reactance X_L at frequency f:
X_L = ωL = 2πfL. Increases with f (inductor blocks high frequencies).
Power of combination of lenses in contact:
P = P₁ + P₂ + ... Equivalent to single lens. Used in corrective lenses (combination).
X-rays: electrons accelerated through high V strike target (Cu, Mo). Bremsstrahlung + characteristic X-rays.
Electric power dissipated in resistor R with current I:
P = I²R = V²/R = VI. Three equivalent forms. Heat dissipated = P×t (Joule's law).
Resistivity of a conductor with increase in temperature:
Conductors: more lattice vibrations → more electron scattering → higher R. Semiconductors: opposite.

Photovoltaic effect: photons create electron-hole pairs in PN junction → current. Renewable energy source.
Standing wave has nodes and antinodes. Distance between consecutive nodes:
Adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart. Adjacent antinodes also λ/2 apart. Node-to-antinode = λ/4.
EM spectrum (low to high freq): Radio, Microwave, IR, Visible, UV, X-rays, Gamma. Gamma from nuclear reactions.
Eddy currents: circular currents in bulk conductor when flux changes. Cause heating (Foucault currents).
Electric potential at distance r from point charge q:
V = kq/r. Scalar quantity. Reference V(∞) = 0. Work per unit charge to bring test charge from infinity.

F = μ_s × N = 0.4 × 50 = 20 N. Body starts moving when applied force exceeds this.
Two capacitors 3 μF and 6 μF in parallel. Equivalent capacitance:
Parallel: C = C₁+C₂ = 3+6 = 9 μF. Same voltage across both; charges add.

∮ E·dA = Q_enclosed/ε₀. Powerful tool for symmetric charge distributions.

Isotones: same N (neutrons), different Z. Example: ¹⁴C (Z=6, N=8) and ¹⁵N (Z=7, N=8).
KE of 1 kg body moving at 10 m/s:
KE = (1/2)mv² = 0.5×1×100 = 50 J. Same as work needed to bring body to this speed.

Shunt: most current bypasses galvanometer. Extends range. Ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
AC generator works on principle of:
Mechanical energy rotates coil in magnetic field → changing flux → induced EMF. Converts mechanical to electrical.

Disconnected → Q constant. C becomes KC, so V = Q/C = V₀/K. Energy decreases by K (since U = Q²/(2C)).

In water, λ' = λ/n. So β' = β/n = β × 3/4. Fringes get closer in denser medium.

Constructive: path diff = nλ (phase diff 2nπ). Destructive: path diff = (n+1/2)λ.

Mirror formula (Cartesian sign convention). f = focal length. Concave: f < 0; Convex: f > 0.
Refractive index of medium with speed of light v:
n = c/v. For vacuum n = 1. For water n = 4/3 ≈ 1.33. For glass n ≈ 1.5. Higher n → slower light.

ν₀ = W/h = 2/(4.14×10⁻¹⁵) = 4.83×10¹⁴ Hz. Below this frequency, no photoemission regardless of intensity.
Torque required to give angular acceleration 4 rad/s² to body with I = 2 kg·m²:
τ = Iα = 2×4 = 8 N·m. Rotational analog of F = ma.
Two capacitors 3 μF and 6 μF in series. Equivalent capacitance:
Series: 1/C = 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2. C = 2 μF. Less than smallest. Same charge on each.
Galvanometer can be converted to voltmeter by connecting:
Series R extends voltage range. Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance (no current draw).
Percentage error in volume of a sphere if radius has 2% error:
V = (4/3)πr³ → ΔV/V = 3(Δr/r) = 3×2% = 6%. Power law amplifies error.
In intrinsic semiconductor at 0 K, conductivity:
At 0 K: no thermal excitation → no free carriers → insulator. Conductivity increases with temperature.
Maximum number of electrons in shell with principal quantum number n:
Max electrons = 2n². For n=1: 2 (K), n=2: 8 (L), n=3: 18 (M), n=4: 32 (N).
Faraday's law of induction: induced EMF equals:
Rate of change of magnetic flux
EMF = −dΦ/dt. Negative sign = Lenz's law (opposes change). Basis of generators, transformers.
Two tuning forks of 256 Hz and 260 Hz sounded together give beats:
Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = 4 Hz. Listener hears 4 intensity maxima per second.

Magnetic field inside a solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current I:
B = μ₀nI inside solenoid (uniform, parallel to axis). Field is zero outside ideal solenoid.
Time for half of sample to decay
t₁/₂ = 0.693/λ. After each half-life, half of remaining atoms decay. Independent of initial amount.

Q = mL = 1000×540 = 5,40,000 cal = 540 kcal. Phase change at constant temperature.

Potential at center of square with 4 charges +q at corners (side a):
Distance from center to each corner = a/√2. V = 4 × kq/(a/√2) = 4√2 kq/a.
A stone tied to string of length 1 m is whirled in vertical circle. Minimum velocity at top to complete loop (g=10):
v_min at top = √(gr) = √(10×1) = √10 m/s. Tension becomes zero, gravity provides centripetal force.
Resistance of wire of length L, area A, resistivity ρ:
R = ρL/A. Longer wire = more R, thicker wire = less R. ρ is material property.
Photocell: incident light → photoelectrons → current. Used in light meters, automatic doors, solar cells.

Perpendicular to each other and to propagation direction
EM wave is transverse. E ⊥ B ⊥ propagation direction. Right-hand rule for orientation.
After 4 half-lives, fraction of radioactive sample remaining:
(1/2)⁴ = 1/16. After n half-lives: (1/2)ⁿ remains. Exponential decay.
Angular momentum of body with I = 2 kg·m² rotating at 5 rad/s:
L = Iω = 2×5 = 10 kg·m²/s. Conserved in absence of external torque.

On perpendicular bisector of dipole: distances equal, potentials cancel. V = 0 (but E ≠ 0).

PE = mgh = 2×10×5 = 100 J. Conservative force; path independent.

B = μ₀I/(2πr). Decreases as 1/r. Reason for high B near power lines.
Isobars: same A, different Z. Example: ⁴⁰Ar, ⁴⁰Ca, ⁴⁰K. Different elements, same mass number.

NAND (NOT-AND) is universal. Similarly NOR. All other gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) can be built from NANDs.

Mayer's relation: CP − CV = R. For monatomic gas: CP = (5/2)R, CV = (3/2)R.

Electric field at center of equilateral triangle with three equal +q charges at corners:
By symmetry, fields from three equal charges cancel at center. Net E = 0.

In inductor: V leads I by 90° (or I lags V). Due to Lenz's law opposing change.
Rayleigh scattering by air molecules. Shorter wavelengths (blue) scatter more than red.
Star light refracted by varying density atmosphere → apparent position shifts → twinkling. Planets don't twinkle (larger angular size).

Min angular resolution = 1.22λ/D (D = aperture). Larger aperture → better resolution.
Image formed by concave mirror when object is between F and pole:
Object between F and P → image virtual, erect, magnified, behind mirror. Used as shaving mirror.

F = kq₁q₂/r² = 9×10⁹ × 1×1/1 = 9×10⁹ N. Massive force (1 C is huge charge).
Image formed by plane mirror is:
Plane mirror: virtual image (behind mirror), erect, same size, same distance. Left-right reversed.
Angle of friction when μ = 1 is:
tan θ = μ = 1 → θ = 45°. Angle of friction = angle of repose for same μ.
Energy stored in inductor L carrying current I:
U = (1/2)LI². Same form as capacitor (1/2)CV². Stored in magnetic field.

β = λD/d. λ = wavelength, D = slit-to-screen distance, d = slit separation.
Potential gradient is related to electric field by:
E = −dV/dx. Field points from high to low potential. Negative gradient.
Why does the sun appear flattened at sunset?
Atmosphere refracts sunlight. Lower part (closer to horizon) refracts more → appears flattened. Visible even when actually below horizon.
A body falling from height h takes 3 s to reach ground. The height is (g = 10 m/s²):
h = (1/2)gt² = 0.5 × 10 × 9 = 45 m. Final velocity v = gt = 30 m/s.
Molar specific heat CV of diatomic gas at room temperature:
5 DOF (3 translational + 2 rotational) at room T → CV = (5/2)R. Vibrational modes frozen.
Echo is heard if reflecting surface is at minimum distance:
Echo distinct from original sound if gap ≥ 0.1 s. Distance = v×t/2 = 340×0.1/2 = 17 m.
Energy density in electric field of intensity E:
u = (1/2)ε₀E². Stored in electric field. Same form as magnetic energy density (1/2)B²/μ₀.
Electric field due to infinite plane sheet with surface charge density σ:
E = σ/(2ε₀). Independent of distance! Two oppositely charged sheets give E = σ/ε₀ between them.
Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) is based on conservation of:
KCL: Σ I at node = 0. Charge doesn't accumulate at node. Same as continuity equation.
Sound: longitudinal (compressions/rarefactions) in medium. Cannot travel through vacuum.
A proton moves perpendicular to magnetic field B with velocity v. Radius of circular path:
r = mv/(qB) = p/(qB). Radius depends on momentum. Higher momentum = larger radius.
Speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum:
c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3×10⁸ m/s. Same as speed of light. Light is an EM wave.
Single slit diffraction: central maximum width depends on:
Angular width of central max = 2λ/a. Linear width on screen = 2λD/a. Narrower slit = wider pattern.
A 0.5 kg ball hits wall at 10 m/s and rebounds at 6 m/s. Impulse by wall (in magnitude):
J = Δp = m(v₂−v₁) = 0.5(6−(−10)) = 0.5×16 = 8 N·s. Direction of impulse reversed.
Frequency of X-rays to atomic number
√ν = a(Z − b). Established atomic number (Z) as fundamental property. Led to modern periodic table.

At resonance: X_L = X_C → cancel. Z = √(R² + 0) = R. Minimum impedance, maximum current.

Three 6 Ω resistors in parallel give:
1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. R = 2 Ω. Three identical in parallel = R/n.
Light waves can be polarized because they are:
Polarization is exclusive property of transverse waves. Longitudinal waves cannot be polarized.

De Broglie wavelength of particle of momentum p:
λ = h/p = h/(mv). Wave-particle duality. Verified by Davisson-Germer electron diffraction experiment.

g' = gR²/(R+h)² = gR²/(2R)² = g/4. Inverse square law for gravity.

Entropy of universe in spontaneous process:
Spontaneous processes are irreversible → entropy of universe increases. ΔS_universe > 0.
Magnetic force on a moving charge is given by:
Lorentz force: F = q(E + v × B). Magnetic part perpendicular to both v and B. No work done.
Capacitive reactance X_C at frequency f:
X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/(2πfC). Decreases with f (capacitor passes high frequencies).
Three 6 Ω resistors in series give:
R = R₁+R₂+R₃ = 6+6+6 = 18 Ω. Same current flows through each.
In isothermal process, ΔU for ideal gas equals:
Isothermal: ΔT = 0 → ΔU = 0 (U depends only on T). All heat added = work done.
Magnetic flux through area A perpendicular to field B:
Φ = BA cos θ. θ = 0 (perpendicular) → Φ = BA. θ = 90° (parallel to surface) → Φ = 0.
Image formed by concave mirror when object is at C (center of curvature):
At C, real, inverted, same size
Object at C → image at C, real, inverted, same size. Used to verify mirror formula.
Electric field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium:
Inside conductor: free charges redistribute to cancel internal field. All charge on surface.
Hard X-rays: high frequency, high energy, more penetrating. Soft X-rays: lower energy, less penetrating.
C-14 (half-life 5730 years) formed in atmosphere by cosmic rays. Living things maintain C-14/C-12 ratio. Stops at death.
Refraction and total internal reflection in raindrops
Light enters raindrop (refracts), reflects internally (TIR), exits (refracts again). Dispersion creates colors.
Orbital velocity near Earth's surface (R = 6.4×10⁶ m, g = 9.8):
v_o = √(gR) = √(9.8×6.4×10⁶) = 7.9 km/s. First cosmic velocity, less than escape velocity.
In adiabatic expansion, temperature of gas:
Q = 0, so W = −ΔU. Gas does work at expense of internal energy. ΔU < 0 → ΔT < 0.
Force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field:
F = BIL sin θ. θ = angle between current direction and B. Maximum when perpendicular, zero when parallel.
Electric field due to infinite line charge λ at perpendicular distance r:
Gauss law with cylinder around line: E×2πrL = λL/ε₀ → E = λ/(2πε₀r). Falls as 1/r.
Photon: quantum (packet) of EM energy. E = hν. Massless, carries momentum and energy. Wave-particle duality.
Escape velocity from Earth's surface (R = 6400 km, g = 9.8 m/s²):
v_e = √(2gR) = √(2×9.8×6.4×10⁶) = 11.2 km/s. Independent of body's mass.
Mode of heat transfer through vacuum:
Radiation doesn't need medium (EM waves). How Sun's energy reaches Earth.
Temperature of normal human body in Kelvin (37°C):
T(K) = T(°C) + 273 = 37 + 273 = 310 K. Body temperature varies slightly throughout day.
Stefan's law: P = σAeT⁴. For ideal black body, e = 1. Real objects have e < 1.
Adiabatic process: relation between P and V:
Adiabatic: PV^γ = constant where γ = CP/CV. No heat exchange (Q = 0).

LED: forward-biased PN junction emits light when electrons and holes recombine. Energy released as photons.
Accommodation of eye is due to:
Ciliary muscles relax (lens thin, distant vision) or contract (lens thick, near vision). Presbyopia: muscles weaken with age.

RP = 1/d_min where d_min = λ/(2μ sin θ). Smaller λ → better RP. Electron microscope: λ very small, very high RP.
Quantum numbers: n (principal), l (azimuthal), m (magnetic), s (spin). For n=3, possible l values:
l = 0 to n−1. For n=3: l = 0(s), 1(p), 2(d). Each l has (2l+1) m values.
Combination of identical capacitors: 3 capacitors in parallel give 12 μF each:
Parallel total = sum = 3C = 12 → C = 4 μF each.
Terminal velocity of a sphere in viscous fluid depends on:
v_t ∝ r². Stokes' law: v_t = 2r²(ρ−σ)g/(9η). Larger drops fall faster (raindrops).
Radius of n-th Bohr orbit of H:
r_n = n² × a₀ = n² × 0.529 Å. Larger n → much larger orbit (cubic dependence on volume).
Maximum KE of photoelectrons depends on:
KE_max = hν − W. Independent of intensity (which affects only number of photoelectrons). Wave theory failed here.

C = K·C₀ when dielectric fills entire space. Charge increases by K (since Q = CV, V constant).

P = P₀ + ρgh = 10⁵ + 1000×10×10 = 2×10⁵ Pa. Gauge pressure = 10⁵ Pa.
Time period of spring-mass system with k = 100 N/m, m = 1 kg:
Pitch is perception of frequency. Higher frequency = higher pitch. Loudness depends on amplitude.
Magnetic field at center of circular coil of radius R, current I, N turns:
B = μ₀NI/(2R). More turns or higher current → stronger field. Smaller coil → stronger field at center.
Drift velocity of electrons in conductor is of order:
Drift velocity ~mm/s (very slow). But electric signal propagates ~10⁸ m/s (close to c).
Electric field at distance r from point charge q:
E = kq/r². Vector pointing away from +q, toward −q. Units: N/C or V/m.
Optical fiber works on principle of:
TIR keeps light bouncing inside fiber core. Used in telecommunications (high bandwidth).
Average KE of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas at temperature T:
3 translational DOF → (3/2)RT per mole. Per molecule: (3/2)kT.
Which radiation has highest ionizing power?
α: heavy, slow → most ionization (10⁴× γ). But lowest penetration (stopped by paper).
At resonance, amplitude is maximum. Driving force reinforces natural oscillation. Examples: swing, tuning forks.
Power factor in LCR series circuit at resonance:
At resonance: X_L = X_C, Z = R. cos φ = R/Z = R/R = 1. Maximum power transfer.
Binding energy per nucleon is maximum for:
BE/A peaks around A=56 (Fe). Fusion releases energy for A<56, fission for A>56. Both approach Fe.
Defect of eye where image forms in front of retina (cannot see far):
Myopia: eyeball too long or lens too strong. Corrected by concave lens (diverging).
Critical angle for total internal reflection (TIR) from medium n₁ to n₂ (n₁ > n₂):
sin c = n₂/n₁. Beyond critical angle, TIR occurs. Used in optical fibers, prisms.
Speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately:
At 0°C: 332 m/s. Increases ~0.6 m/s per °C. At 20°C: ~344 m/s.
A stone is dropped from a tower and reaches ground in 4 s. Height of tower (g=10):
h = (1/2)gt² = 0.5×10×16 = 80 m. Velocity at impact = gt = 40 m/s.
Work done in moving charge q through potential difference V:
W = qV. Units: joules (C × V). Same as energy gained/lost by charge.
Potentiometer measures EMF without drawing current. Sensitivity depends on:
Longer wire = more sensitivity (smaller potential gradient). Higher driver EMF needed for longer wire.
Malus's law: intensity after polarizer at angle θ:
For polarized light through analyzer: I = I₀ cos²θ. θ = angle between polarizer axes.

Power needed to lift 50 kg at constant velocity 2 m/s (g = 10):
P = Fv = mgv = 50×10×2 = 1000 W = 1 kW. Equal to change in PE per second.
Latent heat of vaporization is generally higher than latent heat of fusion because:
Phase change involves more bond breaking
Vaporization breaks intermolecular bonds completely (large energy). Fusion only loosens the lattice (smaller energy).
Doppler effect: source approaches observer with velocity. Apparent frequency:
Approaching source: f' > f (waves compressed). Receding source: f' < f.
A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s². Distance covered in 5 s:
s = ut + (1/2)at² = 0 + 0.5×2×25 = 25 m. Final velocity = at = 10 m/s.

I_rms = I_max/√2 = 10/1.414 = 7.07 A. Frequency = 100π/(2π) = 50 Hz (Indian standard).

Pentavalent: 5 valence electrons. 4 bond with Si, 1 free → electron majority carriers. Donor impurity.

eV_s = KE_max → V_s = KE_max/e. Measures max KE; in volts, equals KE in eV.

Defect of eye where image forms behind retina (cannot see near):
Hypermetropia: eyeball too short or lens weak. Corrected by convex lens (converging).

Sun appears reddish at sunrise/sunset because:
Rayleigh scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴. Blue scatters more (sky blue). Red penetrates through long atmospheric path.
Mass-energy equivalence E = mc² was proposed by:
Einstein's special relativity (1905). 1 u = 931.5 MeV. Basis of nuclear energy release.
Series of H-spectrum in visible region:
Balmer: transitions to n=2. Visible (400-700 nm). First identified by Balmer (1885).

Sound speed: air 340 m/s, water 1500 m/s (4.4×), steel 5000 m/s. Solids faster due to closer molecules.

For floating: ρ_body × V = ρ_water × V_sub → ρ_body = 0.8×1000 = 800 kg/m³. Wood-like.

v_rms ∝ √T. To double: T must be 4×300 = 1200 K.

For l=0 (s): 2; l=1 (p): 6; l=2 (d): 10; l=3 (f): 14. Two electrons per orbital (spin up/down).

V = E − Ir. As I increases, voltage drop across internal resistance increases. Battery weakens under load.

p = E/c = hν/c = h/λ. Photon has zero rest mass but nonzero momentum (relativistic).

E = σT⁴. Stefan-Boltzmann law. σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W/m²·K⁴. Hot objects radiate dramatically more.

Zn loses electrons (oxidized) → reducing agent. Cu²⁺ gains electrons (reduced) → oxidizing agent.

d-d transitions between split d-orbitals absorb visible light. Color = complement of absorbed. Examples: Cu²⁺ blue, Fe²⁺ green.

Phenoxide stabilized by resonance (charge delocalized into ring). Alkoxide has no such stabilization.

Chloroplast: plant organelle for photosynthesis. Contains chlorophyll. Bacteria have chromatophores instead.
Ferns: Pteridophyta. Vascular (xylem/phloem). Spores on sori (underside of leaves). Examples: Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum.
Funaria: moss (Bryophyta). Leafy gametophyte + sporophyte (capsule on seta). Capsule releases spores. Requires moist habitat.
Dihybrid (two traits): 9 (both dominant) : 3 (one dom, one rec) : 3 (one rec, one dom) : 1 (both recessive). Assumes independent assortment.
Gymnosperms: first seed plants ('naked seeds', no fruit). Conifers, cycads, Ginkgo, Gnetum. Predominant in colder regions.
Kranz: wreath-like arrangement. Mesophyll + large bundle sheath cells with chloroplasts. Two-step CO₂ fixation. C₄ plants.
Bacteria are prokaryotes, lack membrane-bound organelles. Use mesosomes (infoldings) for respiration.
Food chain: producers (plants/algae) → primary consumers (herbivores) → secondary → tertiary → quaternary. Energy flows from sun → producers.
Dicots: 2 cotyledons (bean, pea). Monocots: 1 cotyledon (scutellum in grasses). Cotyledons store food or absorb from endosperm.
Nitrification: NH₃ → NO₂⁻ (Nitrosomonas) → NO₃⁻ (Nitrobacter). Aerobic. Makes nitrogen available to plants (nitrates easily absorbed).
Stroma: CO₂ fixation by RuBisCO. Calvin cycle: 3 phases - carboxylation, reduction, regeneration. Forms G3P → glucose.
Ampulla: widest part of fallopian tube. Sperm meets egg ~12-24 hrs after ovulation. Zygote → morula → blastocyst → implants in uterus.
Splitting of water in photosynthesis is called:
Photolysis: H₂O → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ + ½O₂. Light energy splits water in PSII. Oxygen released from water, not CO₂.
Zygote (2n) → embryo. Stages: proembryo → globular → heart-shaped → torpedo → mature embryo (with radicle, plumule, cotyledons).
Cyclic: electrons cycle from PSI back to PSI via ETC. Produces only ATP (no NADPH, no O₂). Common in bacteria.
Fermentation produces how many ATP per glucose?
Fermentation (anaerobic): only glycolysis. 2 ATP per glucose. Inefficient but allows survival without O₂.
ABA: 'stress hormone'. Closes stomata during water stress (reduces transpiration). Inhibits growth. Promotes seed dormancy.
Cross of F₁ with either parent
Back cross: F₁ × either parent. Test cross is special case (with recessive parent). Useful in plant breeding to introgress traits.
Cuticle: waxy layer on epidermis. Cutin (polymer of fatty acids). Prevents water loss. Thicker in xerophytes (cactus).
Pine: gymnosperm. Cones (male + female), naked seeds (in cones), needle-like leaves (xerophytic), evergreen. Softwood.
Pollen grain: immature male gametophyte (microgametophyte). 2 cells (vegetative + generative) or 3 cells (vegetative + 2 sperm) at maturity.
Restriction endonucleases: cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences. 'Molecular scissors'. Found in bacteria (defense vs phages). Used in recombinant DNA technology.
Pituitary (hypophysis): controls other endocrine glands via tropic hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, GH). Posterior stores ADH, oxytocin.
Bt cotton: contains gene from Bacillus thuringiensis. Produces Cry protein (Bt toxin) → kills cotton bollworm. Specific to insects, safe for humans.
Cambium: lateral meristem. Vascular cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem. Cork cambium (phellogen) produces periderm.
Genes on same chromosome always link
Genes on different chromosomes assort independently
Independent assortment: genes on different chromosomes inherited independently. Meiosis I (random chromosome alignment). Not true for linked genes.
Inability of pollen to fertilize same flower/genotype
Self-incompatibility: biochemical recognition prevents self-pollen from fertilizing. Promotes outcrossing. Common in crucifers, sunflower.
Plant cell division differs from animal cell division in:
Plants: lack centrioles, form cell plate. Animals: centrioles present, cleavage furrow. Both have spindle, mitosis stages.
Plants: cell plate forms from Golgi vesicles at center, grows outward → cell wall. Animals: cleavage furrow (actin-myosin).
Intercalary: at base of internodes or leaves. Allows growth in length after apical meristem differentiation. Common in grasses (mowing tolerant).
Companion cells: small, nucleated cells next to sieve tubes. Provide proteins/ATP to enucleate sieve tubes. Assist loading/unloading.
Decomposers (saprotrophs): bacteria, fungi. Break down dead organic matter, release nutrients (N, P, C) back to soil. Critical for nutrient cycling.
Which enzyme can act as both carboxylase and oxygenase?
RuBisCO: dual activity. With CO₂ → carboxylation (Calvin). With O₂ → oxygenation (photorespiration, wasteful).
Pteridophytes (ferns): first vascular plants (xylem + phloem). No seeds (spore dispersal). Examples: ferns, horsetails, clubmosses.
Chloroplast: organelle in plant cells. Light reactions in thylakoid, dark (Calvin) in stroma.
Number of ATP needed to synthesize 1 glucose in C₃:
C₃: 6 turns of Calvin cycle for 1 glucose. Each turn: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH. Total: 18 ATP + 12 NADPH per glucose.
LDP: flower when day length exceeds critical duration (summer). Examples: spinach, radish, wheat. SDP: chrysanthemum, soybean (autumn).
Vascular bundle: xylem (water/minerals, inside) + phloem (food, outside). Sometimes cambium (lateral meristem) between them.
Mutation: change in DNA sequence. Types: point (substitution), frameshift (insertion/deletion), chromosomal. Causes: radiation, chemicals, errors.
Krebs: mitochondrial matrix. Pyruvate → Acetyl-CoA → TCA cycle. Produces CO₂, NADH, FADH₂, 2 ATP per glucose.
Regions with high endemic + threatened species
Hotspots: 36 globally (Myers, 1988; updated). Criteria: ≥1500 endemic plant species, ≥70% habitat loss. Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland in India region.
RQ = CO₂ produced / O₂ consumed. Carbohydrates: 1.0 (equal). Fats: 0.7 (less CO₂). Proteins: 0.8-0.9.
ETS (electron transport chain) is located in:
ETS: inner mitochondrial membrane. Complexes I-IV + ATP synthase. Electrons from NADH/FADH₂ → O₂. Proton gradient drives ATP.
Ecological pyramid: graphic of trophic structure. Types: number, biomass, energy. Inverted pyramids (number) possible in forests (many insects, few trees).
ABO blood group is example of:
ABO: 3 alleles in population (I^A, I^B, i). I^A and I^B codominant, both dominant over i. Multiple alleles + codominance.
Plant tissue responsible for secondary growth:
Secondary growth (girth): vascular cambium (between xylem/phloem) + cork cambium (replaces epidermis). Found in dicots.
Decomposers (saprotrophs): bacteria, fungi. Break down dead organic matter → release inorganic nutrients back to soil. Nutrient cycling.
Carbon reservoirs: atmosphere (CO₂), oceans (largest active), fossil fuels, sedimentary rocks. Photosynthesis removes CO₂, respiration/combustion adds.
Presence/absence of vascular tissue, seeds, flowers
Classification: vascular tissue (present/absent), seed (present/absent), fruit (present/absent), flower (present/absent).
Law of segregation (Mendel's First Law): each gamete receives one allele of each gene. Meiosis I (anaphase I) physically separates homologous chromosomes.
Neuron: ~86 billion in brain. Parts: dendrites (input), cell body, axon (output). Synapse: junction between neurons.
Increasing concentration of toxins in higher trophic levels
Biomagnification: fat-soluble toxins (DDT, mercury, PCBs) concentrate up food chain. Top predators (eagles, humans) accumulate highest levels. Threatens species.
1% recombination = 1 centimorgan (cM) = 1 map unit. Used to construct genetic maps. Higher RF = farther apart. Max RF = 50% (independent assortment).
Light reactions of photosynthesis occur in:
Thylakoids: photosystems, ETC, ATP synthase. Light absorbed, water split, ATP & NADPH produced.
First stable product of CO₂ fixation in C₄ plants:
C₄: PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ to PEP (3C) → OAA (4C). Kranz anatomy (mesophyll + bundle sheath cells). Corn, sugarcane.
Secondary succession: disturbance (fire, flood, abandoned farm) → soil remains → faster than primary. Pioneer: grasses, weeds. Reaches climax in decades.
Megasporogenesis: megaspore mother cell (2n) → meiosis → 4 megaspores (linear tetrad). Only 1 (chalazal) functional → develops into embryo sac.
Integuments → seed coat. Outer: testa (hard). Inner: tegmen (thin). Micropyle remains (water entry, gas exchange). Hilum: scar of attachment.
Guard cells: when turgid (water enters due to K⁺ influx), stomata open. When flaccid, stomata close. Light + low CO₂ trigger opening.
Annual rings in trees are due to:
Seasonal variation in activity of cambium
Spring wood (early wood): large vessels, less dense. Autumn wood (late wood): smaller, denser. One ring per year. Used in dendrochronology.
Xylem and phloem on same radius
Xylem and phloem on different radii
Conjoint: xylem + phloem on same radius (typical of stems). Collateral: side by side. Bicollateral: phloem on both sides of xylem.
Pteridophytes (ferns): first vascular plants (xylem + phloem). No seeds (spore dispersal). Examples: ferns, horsetails, clubmosses.
Test cross is used to determine:
Test cross: cross with homozygous recessive. If offspring all dominant → parent homozygous dominant. If 1:1 ratio → heterozygous.
Penetrance: % of individuals with genotype who express phenotype. Complete (100%) vs incomplete (e.g., BRCA mutations ~80%). Expressivity: variation in severity.
Photosynthesis dark reaction is also called:
Calvin cycle (C₃ cycle): CO₂ fixation in stroma. RuBisCO enzyme. 3 phases: carboxylation, reduction, regeneration. Forms G3P → glucose.
N deficiency: chlorosis (yellowing) starting from older leaves. N mobile, moves to young leaves. Essential for chlorophyll, proteins.
Total ATP from one glucose (aerobic respiration):
Complete oxidation: 2 (glycolysis) + 2 (GTP in TCA) + 34 (oxidative phosphorylation) = 38 ATP. Actual: ~30-32 due to transport costs.
Trophic level: each step in food chain. Producers (level 1), primary consumers (2), secondary (3), etc. Decomposers operate across all levels.
X-linked recessive: males more affected (only 1 X). Females carriers. Examples: color blindness, hemophilia, Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Primary CO₂ acceptor in C₄ plants:
C₄: PEP (3C) + CO₂ → OAA (4C). PEP carboxylase has high affinity for CO₂, no oxygenase activity.
Phytochrome is a plant pigment involved in:
Phytochrome (P_R and P_FR): photoreceptor for red/far-red light. Regulates flowering, seed germination, shade avoidance. Switches forms.
Nephron: ~1 million per kidney. Components: Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct. Filtration, reabsorption, secretion.
Casparian strips: band of suberin (waterproof) on radial and tangential walls of endodermis. Forces water through membranes (selective).
Collenchyma: living, thick corners (cellulose + pectin). Flexible support (growing parts). Common in stems, leaf stalks. Example: celery strings.
First stable product of CO₂ fixation in C₃ plants:
C₃ (Calvin): RuBisCO fixes CO₂ to RuBP (5C) → 2× 3-PGA (3C). Hence 'C₃'. Most plants (wheat, rice).
SA node (sinoatrial): right atrium wall. Generates electrical impulses ~70-80/min. Sets heart rhythm. Natural pacemaker.
Mutagens: physical (UV, X-rays, gamma), chemical (mustard gas, nitrous acid, EMS, colchicine). Some are also carcinogens (cause cancer).
In dicot stem, vascular bundles are:
Dicot stem: conjoint, collateral, open (cambium present → secondary growth). Monocot stem: conjoint, collateral, closed (no cambium).
Syngamy: sperm + egg → 2n zygote (future embryo). Triple fusion: sperm + 2 polar nuclei → 3n primary endosperm cell (food storage).
Periderm: phellem (cork, outside) + phellogen (cork cambium, middle) + phelloderm (inside). Replaces epidermis in secondary growth.
Food web: network of interlinked food chains. More stable than single chain (alternative foods). Complexity increases stability.
Apical meristem: growing tips. Produces primary growth (length). Cells divide mitotically → primary tissues (dermal, ground, vascular).
Secondary xylem = wood. Hardwood (dicots) vs softwood (gymnosperms). Annual rings counted to estimate tree age.
Crossing over: pachytene (substage of prophase I, meiosis). Synaptonemal complex allows exchange between homologous chromosomes. Recombination nodules.
Linkage: genes on same chromosome tend to be inherited together. Closely linked → less recombination. Morgan's work with Drosophila.
Compensation point: net gas exchange = 0 (photosynthesis = respiration). Plant neither gains nor loses mass. Below: net loss.
Site of light reaction in chloroplast:
Thylakoid membrane contains chlorophyll, photosystems I & II, ETC, ATP synthase. Light reactions: H₂O split, ATP + NADPH produced.
Angiosperms: flowering plants (seeds enclosed in fruit). Most diverse, dominant. Monocots + dicots. Co-evolved with pollinators.
Apple: false fruit. Edible part develops from thalamus (receptacle), not ovary. True fruit is core (pome). Strawberry, pear similar.
Phellogen develops from outer cortical cells. Produces phellem (cork, outside) and phelloderm (inside). Together form periderm.
Plant hormone that promotes cell elongation:
Auxin (IAA): promotes cell elongation (acid growth hypothesis - cell wall loosens). Also: apical dominance, root initiation, phototropism.
Photophosphorylation: light-driven ATP synthesis. Cyclic (PSI only, makes ATP) and non-cyclic (PSII→PSI, ATP+NADPH+O₂).
Monocots (1 cotyledon, parallel venation): grasses, lilies. Dicots (2 cotyledons, reticulate venation): roses, beans. Major angiosperm groups.
Schleiden (plants, 1838) + Schwann (animals, 1839): all organisms composed of cells. Virchow added 'cells from cells' (1855).
Photorespiration: RuBisCO uses O₂ instead of CO₂. Wastes energy, no ATP. C₃ plants affected; C₄ and CAM minimize.
Chlorenchyma: photosynthetic parenchyma (e.g., mesophyll in leaves). Two types in dicot leaf: palisade (columnar, upper) and spongy (irregular, lower).
Polygenic: trait controlled by multiple genes (additive effect). Continuous variation (bell curve). Examples: height, skin color, intelligence.
Pinus: gymnosperm. Cones (male small + female large). Winged seeds (wind dispersal). Needle leaves (xerophytic).
Non-albuminous (exalbuminous): endosperm consumed during embryo development. Cotyledons store food. Examples: pea, bean, gram.
Geotropism: roots grow down (positive), stems up (negative). Auxin accumulates on lower side. In roots: inhibits elongation → bends down. In stems: promotes → bends up.
Sclerenchyma: dead at maturity, thick lignified walls. Two types: fibers (long, slender) and sclereids (stone cells, e.g., pear grit).
Heartwood differs from sapwood in being:
Heartwood: older, inner xylem. Cells dead, filled with tannins/resins → darker. Mechanical support only. Sapwood: outer, conducts water.
Excess nutrients causing algal bloom in water bodies
Eutrophication: N/P from fertilizers, sewage → algal bloom → algae die → decomposition → O₂ depleted → fish death. Cultural eutrophication (human-made).
Vessels: short, wide, perforated end walls (efficient water flow). Tracheids: long, narrow, pitted (less efficient). Vessels in angiosperms.
Cycas: gymnosperm. 'Living fossil'. Coralloid roots (with N-fixing cyanobacteria). Crown of leaves. Dioecious.
Plant hormone responsible for cell elongation:
Auxin (IAA): promotes cell elongation (acid growth hypothesis). Also apical dominance, root initiation, parthenocarpy. Discovered by Went (1928).
Lateral meristems (secondary growth): vascular cambium (secondary xylem + phloem), cork cambium (periderm). Increases girth.
Bark: periderm + secondary phloem + cortex. Everything outside vascular cambium. cork cambium (phellogen) produces cork (outside) and phelloderm (inside).
Plant cell wall is mainly composed of:
Cellulose: polymer of β-glucose. Provides rigidity. Plants differ from animals (no cell wall) and fungi (chitin).
N₂ fixation: N₂ → NH₃ by Rhizobium (symbiotic), Azotobacter (free-living), Nostoc (cyanobacteria). Industrial: Haber process. Lightning also fixes.
CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism): stomata open at night (less water loss). CO₂ fixed into malic acid, used in day. Cacti, succulents.
Plant cells connected by plasmodesmata form:
Symplast: continuous cytoplasm through plasmodesmata. Apoplast: cell walls (intercellular spaces). Two water transport routes.
Endodermis in stem is also called:
Stem endodermis: stores starch → 'starch sheath'. Less prominent than in root. Has Casparian strips but not as developed.
Food transport in plants occurs through:
Phloem: sieve tubes (living cells) + companion cells. Translocation (source to sink). Sugar (sucrose) primarily.
Guard cells: when turgid (water enters), stomata open. K⁺ influx → water follows → turgor → open. Reverse to close.
Carpel (female part): stigma (catches pollen) + style (tube) + ovary (contains ovules). Ovule → seed after fertilization.
Phellem: produced by phellogen (cork cambium) outward. Dead, suberized (waterproof). Replaces epidermis in secondary growth. Outer bark.
Primary CO₂ acceptor in C₃ plants:
C₃: RuBP (5C) + CO₂ → 2× 3-PGA (3C). Catalyzed by RuBisCO. Also causes photorespiration (O₂ competes with CO₂).
Monocot root: polyarch (many xylem strands, e.g., 8-20). Dicot root: diarch to hexarch (2-6 strands). Both radial arrangement.
Dicot root: 2-6 xylem strands (rarely more). Monocot root: many strands (12-20+). Xylem exarch (protoxylem outside).
Apical dominance: apical bud suppresses lateral bud growth via auxin. Removing tip → lateral branches grow. Pinching (gardening) uses this.
Monocot leaves: mesophyll not differentiated (uniform). Dicot leaves: palisade (upper, columnar) + spongy (lower, irregular).
Aneuploidy: 2n±1 (trisomy, monosomy). Examples: Down (47, +21), Turner (45, X), Klinefelter (47, XXY). Nondisjunction in meiosis.
Total organic matter fixed by photosynthesis
GPP: total photosynthesis. NPP = GPP - R (plant respiration). NPP is what's stored as biomass, available to ecosystem.
Plasmodesmata: channels through cell walls, connecting cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells. Allow transport, communication.
Involves PSII and PSI (produces ATP, NADPH, O₂)
Non-cyclic: electrons from water → PSII → PSI → NADP⁺. Produces ATP, NADPH, O₂. Standard pathway in plants.
Number of bones in adult human:
Adult: 206 bones. Newborn: ~270-300 (some fuse). Axial: 80 (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum). Appendicular: 126 (limbs, girdles).
Polyploidy: 3n (triploid), 4n (tetraploid), etc. Common in plants (bananas 3n, seedless; wheat 6n hexaploid). Often sterile (no proper meiosis).
Pioneer species: first to colonize. Primary succession (bare rock): lichens (symbiotic fungi+algae) → mosses → grasses → shrubs → trees. Slow.
Which pigment is present in chloroplast?
Chlorophyll a (green, universal in plants, algae, cyanobacteria). Also chlorophyll b, carotenoids, xanthophylls.
Androecium (male): stamens. Gynoecium (female): carpels. Calyx: sepals. Corolla: petals. Complete flower has all 4 whorls.
Cleistogamy: flowers don't open, self-pollinate. Ensures reproduction even without pollinators. Examples: Viola, Oxalis. No variation.
Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts): need water for fertilization (motile sperm). 'Amphibians of plant kingdom'. No true vascular tissue.
Monocots: parallel venation (grass, lily). Dicots: reticulate (net-like) venation (rose, mango). Distinguishing feature of angiosperms.
Pedigree: family tree. Symbols: square (male), circle (female), shaded (affected). Used to determine inheritance pattern: autosomal dominant, recessive, X-linked.
Pores in bark for gas exchange
Lenticels: small pores in bark (periderm). Allow gas exchange when stomata unavailable (woody stems). Often raised spots.
Pyramid of number in forest ecosystem is:
Forest: few trees (huge biomass) → many herbivorous insects → fewer predators. Number pyramid inverted (fewer producers than primary consumers).
Stroma: fluid surrounding thylakoids. Contains Calvin cycle enzymes (RuBisCO), DNA, ribosomes. Site of CO₂ fixation.
Water transport in plants occurs through:
Xylem: water + minerals (root to leaf). Phloem: food (sugar) transport. Xylem has tracheids, vessels (dead cells).
Thylakoids: chlorophyll, photosystems I & II, electron transport chain. Site of light reactions (ATP, NADPH).
Allogamy: transfer of pollen from anther of one flower to stigma of another (different genetic plant). Promotes variation.
Flower with both stamens and carpels:
Bisexual/perfect: both sexes (e.g., rose, hibiscus). Unisexual: one sex only. Staminate: male only. Pistillate: female only.
Number of nuclei in mature angiosperm embryo sac (Polygonum type):
Polygonum type (most common): 8 nuclei in 7 cells. Egg (1) + synergids (2) + antipodals (3) + central cell with 2 polar nuclei (1 cell, 2 nuclei).
Male and female flowers on same plant
Monoecious: both unisexual flowers on same plant (maize, cucumber). Dioecious: male and female on different plants (papaya, date palm).
Chlorophyll absorbs blue and red, reflects/transmits green → we see green. Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR): 400-700 nm.
Perisperm: residual nucellus in seed (often consumed). Examples: black pepper, beet. Functions like endosperm (food storage) but maternal (2n).
Photosystem I (PSI) absorbs light at wavelength:
PSI: reaction center at 700 nm. Receives electrons from PSII (via ETC). Reduces NADP⁺ to NADPH.
Cytokinin (kinetin, zeatin): promotes cell division (cytokinesis). Found in coconut milk, root tips. Delays senescence. Antagonist to auxin.
Vascular bundle in monocot stem is:
Monocot stem: vascular bundles scattered, conjoint, collateral, closed (no cambium). No secondary growth. Dicot stem: ring, open, secondary growth.
Anemophily: wind pollination. Features: light pollen, large anthers, feathery stigma, no scent/color (no need to attract). Maize, grasses.
Trichomes: epidermal outgrowths. Reduce transpiration (shade, trap moisture), defense (sticky/toxic secretions). Cotton fibers are trichomes.
Cyanobacteria: prokaryotes (no nucleus, no membrane-bound organelles). Photosynthetic. Plants, fungi, animals are eukaryotic.
Yeast: glucose → 2 ethanol + 2 CO₂ + 2 ATP. Anaerobic. Used in brewing, baking. Also occurs in plant roots in waterlogged soil.
Monohybrid (one trait): F₂ phenotype ratio 3 dominant : 1 recessive. Genotype ratio: 1 homozygous dominant : 2 heterozygous : 1 homozygous recessive.
Ribosomes: 70S (prokaryotes, chloroplasts, mitochondria) or 80S (eukaryotic cytoplasm). Translate mRNA → protein.
Palisade: columnar parenchyma cells, just below upper epidermis. Rich in chloroplasts. Primary site of photosynthesis.
Mendel's law of segregation is based on:
Segregation: during meiosis I (anaphase I), homologous chromosomes separate → each gamete gets 1 allele. Mendel's First Law.
Vernalization: cold exposure induces flowering. Winter varieties of wheat, rye need cold. Spring varieties don't. Discovered by Lysenko.
Macronutrients for plants include all EXCEPT:
Macronutrients (large amounts): N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S. Micronutrients (small): Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl, Ni.
Gymnosperms (and angiosperms): sporophyte dominant (tree/plant). Gametophyte reduced, dependent on sporophyte (within cones/flowers).
AIDS: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). Retrovirus. Attacks CD4+ T-helper cells → immunodeficiency. Transmitted: sex, blood, mother-to-child.
Final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration:
O₂ accepts electrons (and H⁺) → water. Without O₂, anaerobic respiration (lactic acid or alcoholic fermentation).
Transpiration is loss of water through:
Transpiration: water evaporates from leaf surface via stomata. Creates transpiration pull → water moves up xylem. Cools plant.
Pteridophytes: sporophyte dominant (fern plant). Gametophyte small, independent (prothallus). Both photosynthetic.
Different maturation times of anther and stigma
Dichogamy: anther and stigma mature at different times. Protandry: anther first. Protogyny: stigma first. Prevents self-pollination.
Law of segregation: alleles separate during gamete formation. Each gamete gets 1 allele. Meiosis I (anaphase I) physically separates homologous chromosomes.
Secondary growth in plants is due to:
Secondary growth: vascular cambium + cork cambium (phellogen). Increases girth. Dicot stems, roots. Monocots generally lack.
Insulin: β-cells of islets of Langerhans (pancreas). Lowers blood glucose. Deficiency: Type 1 diabetes. Resistance: Type 2.
Dicots: 2 cotyledons. Other features: reticulate venation, tap root, vascular bundles in ring, secondary growth. Most flowering plants.
Angiosperms: ~3,00,000 species. Most diverse. Adapted to all habitats. Animal pollination, fruit dispersal key innovations.
Vessels: efficient water-conducting xylem cells. Mostly angiosperms. Gymnosperms (conifers) lack vessels (have tracheids only). Some gnetophytes exception.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules contain:
Nitrogenase: N₂ + 8H + 8e⁻ + 16 ATP → 2NH₃ + H₂ + 16ADP. Sensitive to O₂ (protected by leghemoglobin).
Pericycle in roots gives rise to:
Lateral roots + part of vascular cambium
Pericycle: layer inside endodermis. Origin of lateral roots (unlike stem branches). Also contributes to vascular cambium and cork cambium.
Initial: 2 cells. Vegetative (tube cell): grows pollen tube. Generative: divides to form 2 male gametes (sperm). 3-celled pollen in some plants.
Food chain: producers → primary consumers → secondary → tertiary → quaternary. Energy flows from sun → producers → consumers → decomposers.
Ovule → seed. Integuments → seed coat (testa, tegmen). Egg → embryo. Endosperm (3n) → food storage. Whole ovary → fruit.
Mendel's laws of inheritance were formulated using:
Mendel (1866): Pisum sativum (garden pea). Chose 7 contrasting traits. Self-pollinated, easy to grow, true-breeding varieties available.
Autogamy: same flower pollination. Allogamy (cross): different flower. Geitonogamy: same plant different flowers (genetically self).
Energy pyramid: always upright (10% rule). Only ~10% energy transfers to next trophic level. Limits food chain length (usually 4-5 levels max).
Stomatal complex: 2 guard cells (bean-shaped in dicots, dumbbell in grasses) + subsidiary cells (assisting). Stomatal pore between guard cells.
Ethylene (C₂H₄): gaseous hormone. Promotes fruit ripening, senescence, abscission. Used commercially to ripen fruits (banana, mango).
Bulliform cells: large, thin-walled cells in grass leaf epidermis. Lose turgor → leaf rolls (reduces transpiration). Hygroscopic cells.
Site of ATP synthesis in mitochondria:
ATP synthase (F₀F₁ complex): inner membrane. Protons flow through → drives ATP synthesis (Mitchell's chemiosmosis).
Large central vacuole in plant cell is bounded by:
Tonoplast: single membrane surrounding vacuole. Stores water, ions, waste. Maintains turgor pressure.
Incomplete dominance: heterozygote intermediate (e.g., red × white snapdragon → pink). F₂: 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white. Phenotype = genotype ratio.
Ammonification: decomposers break organic N (proteins, urea) → NH₃/NH₄⁺. Releases ammonia from dead organisms, waste. Mineralization.
Monocot (isobilateral leaf): stomata on both sides (vertical leaf orientation). Dicot (dorsiventral): mainly lower surface (less water loss).
ABO: 3 alleles (I^A, I^B, i) in population. Each individual has only 2 (diploid). I^A and I^B codominant over i. Multiple alleles → 6 genotypes, 4 phenotypes.
Interaction of alleles of same gene
Epistasis: one gene masks/modifies expression of another. Example: Labrador coat color (B/b and E/e). Modifier gene. Ratios like 9:3:4, 12:3:1.
Chloroplast: site of photosynthesis (food production). 'Kitchen of cell'. Mitochondria = powerhouse. Plastid family.
NPP = GPP − R. Available to consumers (herbivores, carnivores, decomposers). NPP varies: forests high, deserts low. Coral reefs highest per area.
Bryophytes: gametophyte dominant (photosynthetic, independent). Sporophyte dependent on gametophyte (small, attached).
Rate of biomass production by producers
Primary productivity: rate of organic matter synthesis by photosynthesis. Gross (GPP) - respiration (R) = Net (NPP). NPP available to consumers.
Mendel used which plant for his experiments?
Garden pea (Pisum sativum): easy to grow, self-pollinated, true-breeding varieties, contrasting traits. Mendel studied 7 traits (1865).
Fruit derived from single flower is:
True fruit: from single flower, single ovary (pea, mango). Aggregate: single flower, many ovaries (raspberry). Multiple: many flowers (pineapple).
Primary succession: bare substrate (rock, sand, lava). Slow (thousands of years). Pioneer: lichens, mosses. Soil forms gradually. Secondary: soil present (after fire, etc.).
Biological nitrogen fixation is done by:
Rhizobium: symbiotic in legume root nodules. Converts N₂ → NH₃ (nitrogenase enzyme). Saves chemical fertilizers.
Chlorophyll a: absorption peaks at 430 (blue) and 662 nm (red). Reflects green (500-570 nm) → plants appear green.
Flower: modified shoot (homology). Sepals, petals modified leaves. Stamens, carpels modified sporophylls (spore-bearing leaves).
Microsporogenesis: anther. Microspore mother cells (2n) → meiosis → 4 microspores (pollen). Each microspore → pollen grain (male gametophyte).
Hooke (1665): observed cork under microscope, saw box-like structures → called 'cells' (monk's rooms). Actually dead cell walls.
Algae: Plantae (multicellular forms like seaweeds) or Protista (unicellular like Chlamydomonas). Photosynthetic, aquatic. No true tissues.
Embryo sac: female gametophyte (megagametophyte). 7 cells, 8 nuclei: egg apparatus (egg + 2 synergids), 3 antipodals, central cell (2 polar nuclei).
Pressure flow (Munch): sugar loaded at source → high solute conc → water enters → high pressure. Phloem sap flows to sink (low pressure).
Humans: ureotelic (excrete urea). Urea: less toxic than ammonia, less water needed. Made in liver (urea cycle). Excreted by kidneys.
Ovary → fruit. Ovary wall (pericarp) → fruit wall (epicarp, mesocarp, endocarp). Ovules → seeds. Fruit protects seeds, aids dispersal.
Number of ATP needed to synthesize 1 glucose in C₄:
C₄: extra ATP for CO₂ concentrating mechanism (PEP regeneration). 12 ATP + 12 NADPH per glucose via Calvin + 12 ATP extra = 30 ATP total.
Bryophytes: first land plants (still need water for reproduction). Pteridophytes: first true vascular land plants. Gymnosperms: first seed plants.
Chromosome theory of inheritance was proposed by:
Sutton-Boveri (1902-1903): chromosomes carry genes. Mendel's laws explained by chromosome behavior in meiosis. Morgan proved with Drosophila.
Unisexual: either male (staminate) or female (pistillate). Maize: monoecious (both on same plant). Papaya: dioecious (separate plants).
Epiblema (root epidermis) differs from stem epidermis:
Epiblema: outermost layer of root. Has root hairs (absorb water). No cuticle (water absorption), no stomata (underground).
Dicots: vascular cambium + cork cambium → secondary growth (girth). Monocots generally lack lateral meristem (exceptions: Dracaena, Yucca).
Plant cell organelle not found in animal cell:
Plastids: chloroplasts (photosynthesis), chromoplasts (color), leucoplasts (storage). Animal cells lack plastids.
Fe: immobile. Deficiency shows in young leaves. Chlorophyll synthesis affected (Fe is cofactor). Interveinal chlorosis (veins green).
Mitochondria: site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle, ETC, ATP synthesis). Semiautonomous (own DNA, ribosomes). 'Powerhouse of cell'.
Male and female flowers on different plants
Dioecious: separate male and female plants. Examples: papaya, date palm, cannabis. Ensures cross-pollination (genetic diversity).
Heartwood: older, inner xylem. Dead, filled with tannins, resins. Provides mechanical support. Sapwood (alburnum): outer, living, conducts water.
Climax: end point of succession. Stable, self-maintaining. Example: oak-hickory forest in temperate regions. Species composition stable.
Antibiotics: kill/inhibit bacteria (target cell wall, protein synthesis). NO effect on viruses (use antivirals). Misuse → antibiotic resistance.
Stamen (male part): anther (pollen sacs) + filament (stalk). Anther produces pollen (male gametophyte).
Monocots: 1 cotyledon (scutellum in grasses). Absorbs nutrients from endosperm during germination. Coleoptile (shoot sheath) + coleorhiza (root sheath).
Fats more reduced (more H, less O) than carbohydrates → need more O₂ → RQ < 1. Tripalmitin: 0.7. Calculated from balanced equation.
Phototropism in plants is due to:
Phototropism: auxin moves to shaded side → cells elongate more → bends toward light. Darwin (1880) studied coleoptile. Went isolated auxin.
Plants: various sex determination. Papaya: XY (male XY, female XX). Some bryophytes: X and Y chromosomes. Many plants have hermaphrodite flowers.
6CO₂ + 12H₂O (light, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O. Oxygen released from water (Van Niel, Ruben & Kamen).
Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts): need water for fertilization (motile sperm). 'Amphibians of plant kingdom'. No true vascular tissue.
Mg: central atom of chlorophyll (like Fe in hemoglobin). Also cofactor for many enzymes (ATP, kinases). Deficiency: interveinal chlorosis.
Cohesion (water molecules stick), adhesion (water to xylem walls), transpiration pull → water rises against gravity.
Mycorrhiza: symbiotic fungus-plant root association. Fungi help absorb water/minerals (P especially); plant provides sugars. Ecto and endo.
AB blood group: both A and B antigens expressed (not blended, both fully expressed). Codominance differs from incomplete dominance (intermediate).
Vagus nerve (X): longest cranial nerve. Mixed (sensory + motor). Supplies heart, lungs, stomach. Main parasympathetic nerve.
BOD: oxygen consumed by microbes decomposing organic matter in water. Higher BOD = more pollution. Clean water: BOD < 5 ppm. Sewage: > 300 ppm.
Mitochondria: site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle, ETC). Produces ATP. Semiautonomous (own DNA).
Stomata in plants are mainly located in:
Mainly lower epidermis: reduces water loss (less direct sun). Some plants: both surfaces. Floating leaves: upper only. Aquatic: absent.
Morgan (1910): white-eyed mutant Drosophila. Genes on X chromosome. Linked genes don't follow independent assortment. Mapping possible.
Parthenocarpy: fruit develops without fertilization → no seeds. Examples: banana, seedless grapes. Can be induced by hormones (auxin, GA) for commercial use.
Aerenchyma: parenchyma with large air spaces. Provides buoyancy (aquatic plants) and aeration (waterlogged roots). Hydrophytes.
Site of glycolysis in plant cell:
Glycolysis: cytoplasm. Glucose → 2 pyruvate (3C) + 2 ATP (net) + 2 NADH. Anaerobic (doesn't need O₂).
Endosperm: 3n (triple fusion: 1 sperm + 2 polar nuclei). Nutritive tissue for embryo. In cereals: persists (food). In beans: consumed (cotyledons store).
Albuminous: endosperm persists at maturity. Examples: wheat, rice, maize (cereals), castor, sunflower. Cotyledons may scavenge endosperm during germination.
Gynoecium (pistil): female reproductive part. Made of 1+ carpels. Each carpel: stigma + style + ovary.
Mango (drupe): epicarp (skin), mesocarp (fleshy, edible), endocarp (stony, protects seed). Other drupes: coconut, peach, plum.
Cell wall of fungi is made of:
Fungi cell wall: chitin (N-acetylglucosamine polymer). Plants: cellulose. Bacteria: peptidoglycan. Distinguishing feature.
Biodiversity peaks in tropics (warm, wet, stable). Amazon rainforest has ~10% of world species. Decreases toward poles. Coral reefs also high.
Hydrophily: water pollination. Rare (most aquatic plants use wind/insects). Examples: Vallisneria (water), Zostera (seagrass). Pollen unwettable.
One sperm + egg, other sperm + 2 polar nuclei
Syngamy: sperm + egg → 2n zygote (embryo). Triple fusion: sperm + 2 polar nuclei → 3n endosperm. Unique to angiosperms. Discovered by Nawaschin (1898).
Double fertilization in angiosperms was discovered by:
Nawaschin (1898, lily): one male gamete + egg → zygote (2n); other male gamete + 2 polar nuclei → endosperm (3n). Unique to angiosperms.
Stomata: pores in epidermis (mainly lower leaf surface). Each has 2 guard cells. Allow gas exchange (CO₂ in, O₂ and water vapor out).
Xylem and phloem on different radii
Radial: xylem and phloem alternate on different radii (typical of roots). Found in monocot and dicot roots.
Bile: produced by liver, stored + concentrated in gallbladder. Contains bile salts (emulsify fat), bile pigments (bilirubin). No digestive enzymes.
Chloroplast: double membrane (outer + inner). Plus thylakoid membrane (third system inside). Endosymbiotic origin.
Photosystem II (PSII) absorbs light at wavelength:
PSII: reaction center chlorophyll a absorbs at 680 nm. Splits water, replaces electrons lost by P680. Connected to PSI via ETC.
Entomophily: insect pollination. Features: large colorful flowers, scent, nectar, sticky/spiny pollen. Bees, butterflies. Most flowering plants.
Sieve tubes: phloem conducting cells. Living, enucleate (no nucleus at maturity). Companion cells assist metabolism.
Only 10% energy transfers to next trophic level
Lindemann's 10% law: ~10% energy passes to next level, 90% lost as heat (respiration, etc.). Limits food chain length.
Ribosomes: 70S (prokaryotes, mitochondria, chloroplasts) or 80S (eukaryotic cytoplasm). Translate mRNA → protein. Free or ER-bound (rough ER).
Parenchyma: most common, living, thin cellulose walls. Functions: storage, photosynthesis (chlorenchyma), secretion. Can dedifferentiate.
Plant hormone causing bolting (sudden stem elongation):
Gibberellin: promotes stem elongation (bolting in cabbage). Also breaks seed/bud dormancy, induces maleness, promotes germination.
Plant cells differ from animal cells in having:
Plant: cell wall (cellulose), plastids (chloroplasts), large central vacuole. Both have nucleus, mitochondria, ER, ribosomes.
Tracheids: long, tapering xylem cells. Dead at maturity, lignified walls with pits. Water moves through pits. Found in all vascular plants.
Pharynx: shared by respiratory (air) and digestive (food) systems. Epiglottis covers glottis during swallowing → prevents food entering trachea.
Fats (triglycerides) → fatty acids + glycerol by lipase (bile emulsifies first). Absorbed into lacteals (lymph) as chylomicrons.
Number of pathogens that cause disease:
Pathogen types: bacteria (TB, cholera), viruses (flu, HIV, COVID), fungi (ringworm), protozoa (malaria, amoebiasis), helminths (tapeworm, roundworm).
Platelets (thrombocytes): 7-10 days. ~250,000/mm³. Function: clotting. Adhere to injury → activate → release factors → clot. Made in bone marrow.
hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin): placenta. Maintains corpus luteum → progesterone → maintains pregnancy. Detected in pregnancy tests (urine, blood).
Kidneys: bean-shaped, behind peritoneum (retroperitoneal), on either side of vertebral column at level T12-L3. Right kidney slightly lower (liver above).
Aschelminthes (roundworms): cylindrical, bilateral, pseudocoelomate. Examples: Ascaris (human intestine), Wuchereria (filariasis). Mostly parasites.
Urea cycle (Krebs-Henseleit, liver): converts toxic ammonia (from protein breakdown) to urea (less toxic, excreted by kidneys). 2 NH₃ + CO₂ → urea + H₂O.
Neurotransmitter at synapse in skeletal muscle:
Acetylcholine (ACh) at neuromuscular junction. Released by motor neuron. Binds nicotinic receptors on muscle → contraction. Acetylcholinesterase breaks down ACh.
Landsteiner (1900): ABO blood groups. Later (with Wiener, 1937-40): Rh factor. Nobel Prize 1930. Made blood transfusions safe.
Number of cranial nerves in humans:

12 pairs of cranial nerves: I (olfactory), II (optic), III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), V (trigeminal), VI (abducens), VII (facial), VIII (vestibulocochlear), IX (glossopharyngeal), X (vagus), XI (accessory), XII (hypoglossal).
Myoglobin: oxygen-binding protein in red muscle fibers (slow-twitch). Higher in endurance muscles. Stores O₂ for sustained activity. Dark meat in chicken (legs).
Different species use different parts of resource
Resource partitioning: species divide resource (e.g., warblers at different tree heights). Reduces direct competition. Allows coexistence.
Yellow color of urine is due to:
Urochrome (urobilin): yellow pigment from hemoglobin breakdown. Color varies with concentration (dehydration = darker). Vitamin B makes it fluorescent yellow.
Exponential (geometric): dN/dt = rN. J-shaped. Possible when resources unlimited (rare, short-term). Bacterial growth, invasive species initially.
Appendix: vestigial (remnant of cecum for cellulose digestion in herbivores). Contains lymphoid tissue (minor immune function). Inflammation → appendicitis.
WBC lifespan varies: neutrophils ~6 hours to few days; lymphocytes (B, T memory) years. ~7000/mm³. Function: immunity.
Pancreatic juice: trypsin, chymotrypsin (proteins), lipase (fats), amylase (carbs), nucleases (DNA/RNA). All enzymes. Bicarbonate neutralizes acid.
Logistic: dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K). Sigmoid. Phases: lag, exponential, deceleration, stable (at K). Realistic for most populations in nature.
Which enzyme digests milk protein casein in infants?
Rennin (chymosin): secreted in infants. Curdles milk protein casein → slow release to small intestine. Adults use pepsin (rennin declines with age).
Class of warm-blooded animals with feathers:
Aves: birds. Feathers (modified scales), beak, hollow bones (flight), 4-chambered heart, warm-blooded (endothermic). Oviparous. ~10,000 species.
Echinodermata: unique water vascular system. Tube feet for locomotion, gas exchange, feeding. Starfish, sea urchin, sea cucumber. Marine only.
Peyer's patches: aggregated lymphoid tissue in ileum. Part of GALT (gut-associated lymphoid tissue). Help immune response against intestinal pathogens.
Stapes: ~3 mm. Middle ear. Transmits vibrations from incus to oval window (cochlea). One of three ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes).
Toxin builds up in single organism
Bioaccumulation: toxin accumulates in single organism over time (e.g., mercury in fish). Biomagnification: concentration increases up food chain (top predators highest).
Carrying capacity (K): max sustainable population. Limited by resources (food, water, space). Logistic growth: N approaches K. Overshoot → die-off.
AP peak: ~+30 mV (inside positive). Due to Na⁺ influx (voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open). Overshoots 0. Then K⁺ efflux repolarizes → hyperpolarizes briefly.
Deciduous (milk) teeth: 20. I 2/2, C 1/1, M 2/2 per quadrant. Appear 6 months - 2 years. Replaced by permanent teeth from 6 years.
O₂-Hb dissociation: sigmoid (cooperative binding). Shifts right (releases O₂ easier): high CO₂, low pH, high T, 2,3-BPG (Bohr effect). Left: opposite.
Maximum population an environment can support
Carrying capacity (K): max sustainable population. Limited by resources (food, water, space). Logistic growth: N approaches K. Overshoot → die-off.
Number of eggs ovulated in female lifetime:
~400 eggs ovulated (out of millions at birth, hundreds of thousands at puberty). One per menstrual cycle (~28 days) for ~30-40 years. Rest degenerate (atresia).
TV: volume inhaled/exhaled in normal quiet breathing (~500 mL). Inspiratory reserve (IRV): ~3000 mL. Expiratory reserve (ERV): ~1100 mL. Residual: 1200 mL.
PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction, Mullis 1983): amplifies DNA in vitro. Cycles: denaturation (95°C), annealing (50-65°C), extension (72°C, Taq polymerase).
Number of chromosomes in human sperm:
Sperm: 23 chromosomes (haploid) from meiosis. 22 autosomes + 1 sex chromosome (X or Y). Egg: 23 (always X). Zygote: 46 (diploid).
Enzyme in saliva that digests starch:
Salivary amylase (ptyalin): starts starch digestion in mouth → maltose. pH ~6.8. Inactivated by stomach acid.
ADH (vasopressin): produced in hypothalamus, stored/released by posterior pituitary. Promotes water reabsorption in kidney. Reduces urine output.
5 basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami (savory, MSG). Bitter most sensitive (poison detection). Umami discovered 1908 (Kikunae Ikeda).
AB-positive: has A, B, Rh antigens. Doesn't make antibodies against any. Can receive any blood type. Universal recipient.
PTH: parathyroid. Raises blood Ca²⁺: bone resorption (osteoclasts), kidney reabsorption, vitamin D activation → gut absorption. Crucial for nerve/muscle function.
Rest and digest response is by:
Parasympathetic: rest/digest. ↓HR, ↑digestion, constricts pupils. Uses acetylcholine. Vagus (X) nerve major parasympathetic. Craniosacral outflow.
Number of pairs of ribs in humans:
Ribs: 12 pairs. True (1-7, attached to sternum directly). False (8-10, attached via cartilage). Floating (11-12, no anterior attachment).
Food chain: producers (plants/algae) → primary consumers (herbivores) → secondary → tertiary → quaternary. Energy flows from sun → producers.
Recombinant insulin (1982, first biotech product): human insulin gene in E. coli. Produces insulin identical to human. Replaced animal insulin (allergies).
O-negative: no A/B antigens (no rejection), no Rh (no Rh incompatibility). Universal donor. AB-positive: universal recipient (has all antigens).
OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine): Sabin vaccine. Attenuated live virus. Given orally (drops). Easier than injectable (Salk). Used in WHO eradication program.
Peyer's patches: lymphoid tissue in ileum. Part of GALT (gut-associated lymphoid tissue). Help immune response against intestinal pathogens.
Vertebrae: 33 total. Cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, sacral 5 (fused), coccygeal 4 (fused). At birth: 33 separate. Adult: ~26 movable.
Keystone: crucial for ecosystem structure. Examples: sea otter (eats urchins, protects kelp), wolf (Yellowstone). Remove → ecosystem changes drastically.
Hypothalamus: hunger (lateral) and satiety (ventromedial) centers. Regulate appetite. Blood glucose, hormones (ghrelin, leptin) modulate.
ADH (vasopressin): from posterior pituitary. Makes collecting duct permeable to water → water reabsorbed → concentrated urine. Alcohol inhibits ADH (diuretic).
Sutures: immovable fibrous joints between skull bones. Allow growth in childhood, fuse in adult (cranial sutures). Fontanelles: soft spots in infants.
HCl in stomach is secreted by:
Parietal cells: HCl + intrinsic factor (B12 absorption). Chief: pepsinogen. Mucous: mucus (protects). G cells: gastrin (hormone).
Implantation: uterine wall (endometrium). ~7 days after fertilization. Blastocyst embeds. Endometrium thickens under progesterone to receive.
Adam's apple is part of which structure?
Adam's apple: thyroid cartilage of larynx. More prominent in males (testosterone). Protects vocal cords. Larger → deeper voice.
Sex of child is determined by:
Egg: always X. Sperm: X or Y (50-50). XX → female, XY → male. So father determines sex. XY-bearing sperm are lighter (less DNA) but differences are minimal.
Most synapses chemical: presynaptic releases neurotransmitter (acetylcholine, dopamine, GABA, etc.) → binds postsynaptic receptors → response. Some electrical (gap junctions).
Trophic level: producer (autotroph), primary consumer (herbivore), secondary (carnivore), tertiary, quaternary. Decomposers across all levels.
Vital capacity: max air exhaled after max inhalation. IRV (3000) + TV (500) + ERV (1100) = 4600 mL. Total lung capacity: VC + RV = 5800 mL.
Number of skeletal muscles in human:
Skeletal muscles: ~640 (varies with anatomy). Voluntary. Attached to bones. ~40% of body mass. Smallest: stapedius (ear). Largest: gluteus maximus.
Bohr effect: increased CO₂/H⁺ (active tissue) → Hb affinity for O₂ decreases → more O₂ released to tissues. Reverse in lungs (low CO₂, high pH).
Crypts of Lieberkühn are present in:
Crypts of Lieberkühn (intestinal glands): tubular glands in small and large intestine. Secrete digestive enzymes + mucus. Source of new epithelial cells.
Pepsinogen → pepsin (active) by HCl. Auto-catalysis: pepsin activates more pepsinogen. Prevents self-digestion of chief cells.
Cochlea: snail-shaped inner ear. Contains organ of Corti (hair cells). Sound → vibrations → fluid waves → hair cells bend → nerve impulses → brain.
Residual volume: ~1200 mL. Air remaining after max expiration. Cannot be exhaled. Prevents lung collapse (atelectasis). Maintains gas exchange.
Commensalism: one benefits, other unaffected. Barnacles (whale transport), epiphytes (orchids on trees). Often asymmetry exists (closer inspection reveals cost).
Gestation: ~280 days (40 weeks) from last menstrual period. Trimesters (3 months each). Birth: full-term at 37-42 weeks. Premature: <37 weeks.
Toxin concentration increases up food chain
Biomagnification: fat-soluble toxins (DDT, mercury, PCBs) concentrate up food chain. Top predators (eagles, humans) accumulate highest. Threatens species.
Annelida (ringed worms): metameric segmentation, true coelom. Examples: earthworm (Pheretima), leech (Hirudinaria), sandworm (Nereis). Closed circulation.
Rh⁻ mother + Rh⁺ baby: mother makes anti-Rh antibodies (at birth). Subsequent Rh⁺ babies attacked → hemolytic disease of newborn (erythroblastosis fetalis). Prevention: RhoGAM.
Taste buds: on papillae of tongue (also palate, throat). ~10,000 buds. 5 basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami. Each bud has ~50-100 receptor cells.
Nephron: ~1 million per kidney. Components: Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct. Filtration, reabsorption, secretion.
Brain protection: cranium (skull), meninges (Dura, Arachnoid, Pia mater), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF, shock absorber). Blood-brain barrier protects from toxins.
Cerebellum: 'little brain'. Coordinates voluntary movement, maintains balance, posture. Damage: ataxia (loss of coordination). Alcohol affects.
Bile salts: emulsify fats (break large drops to small → larger surface area for lipase). Also activate pancreatic lipase.
Rennin (chymosin): in infants, curdles milk protein casein → longer retention in stomach for better digestion. Adults: pepsin handles it. Declines with age.
Oxytocin: hypothalamus, released by posterior pituitary. 'Love/bonding hormone'. Uterine contractions (childbirth), milk ejection (nursing), social bonding.
BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin): attenuated Mycobacterium bovis. Given at birth (India). Protects against severe childhood TB. Variable efficacy in adults.
Number of individuals per unit area/volume
Population density (N): individuals per unit area. Affected by: births, deaths, immigration, emigration. N(t+1) = N(t) + B + I − D − E.
Goblet cells: scattered in intestinal epithelium. Secrete mucus → lubricates food, protects mucosa from digestive enzymes.
Malaria: Plasmodium (falciparum, vivax, malariae, ovale). Vector: female Anopheles mosquito. Symptoms: fever, chills, anemia. Malaria is a major killer in tropics.
Porifera: sponges. Simplest animals. Cellular level (no true tissues). Pore-bearing body. Filter feeders. Mostly marine.
Gestation: 280 days from last menstrual period. Divided into 3 trimesters. Full-term: 37-42 weeks. Premature: <37 weeks.
Pituitary: 'master gland'. Controls other endocrine glands via tropic hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, GH, prolactin). Posterior stores ADH, oxytocin.
Nephron: structural + functional unit of kidney. ~1 million per kidney. Components: Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct.
Alveoli: small sacs in lungs (~300 million). Total surface area ~80 m² (tennis court!). Thin walls (1 cell), surrounded by capillaries. Gas exchange.
Cnidaria: radial symmetry, tissue level. Cnidocytes (stinging cells). Two body forms: polyp (sessile) and medusa (free). Examples: Hydra, jellyfish, coral.
Fovea centralis (in macula): pit in center of retina. Only cones, no rods, no blood vessels. Highest visual acuity. Used for reading, color vision.
Number of chromosomes in human gamete:
Human somatic cells: 46 (diploid, 23 pairs). Gametes (sperm/egg): 23 (haploid) from meiosis. 22 autosomes + 1 sex chromosome (X or Y in sperm, X in egg).
Increased CO₂/H⁺ decreases Hb affinity for O₂
Bohr effect: in active tissues (high CO₂, H⁺), Hb affinity for O₂ decreases → more O₂ released. Reverse in lungs (low CO₂) → O₂ binds.
LH (luteinizing hormone): anterior pituitary. Females: triggers ovulation, maintains corpus luteum (progesterone). Males: stimulates Leydig cells (testosterone).
Salivary amylase (ptyalin): starts starch digestion in mouth → maltose. Optimal pH ~6.8. Inactivated by stomach acid.
Respiratory center: medulla (rhythm generation) + pons (regulation). Responds to CO₂ (chemoreceptors in aorta, carotid). Hyperventilation lowers CO₂ → apnea.
Carbon dioxide is transported in blood mainly as:
CO₂ transport: 70% as HCO₃⁻ (formed in RBC via carbonic anhydrase), 23% as carbamino-Hb, 7% dissolved in plasma.
Function of bile in digestion is:
Bile salts emulsify fats: break large fat drops into small droplets → larger surface area for pancreatic lipase. Bile has NO digestive enzymes.
Human Genome Project was completed in:
HGP: started 1990, completed 2003 (50th anniversary of DNA structure). ~3 billion base pairs, ~20,000-25,000 genes. International collaboration.
Normal adult: 120/80 mmHg. Systolic: ventricular contraction. Diastolic: relaxation. Hypertension: >140/90. Hypotension: <90/60.
Renin: from JGA (kidney, when BP low). Triggers RAAS (renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system) → aldosterone → ↑Na⁺/water reabsorption → ↑BP.
Mollusca: mantle (tissue covering visceral mass, secretes shell), muscular foot, radula. Snails, octopus, clams, oysters.
Menstrual cycle: ~28 days (21-35 normal). Day 1: menstruation. Day 14: ovulation. Phases: menstrual (1-5), follicular (1-13), ovulation (14), luteal (15-28).
Rh factor: Rh-negative mother, Rh-positive fetus risk:
Hemolytic disease of newborn (erythroblastosis fetalis): Rh⁻ mother makes anti-Rh antibodies after exposure to Rh⁺ baby (at birth). Subsequent Rh⁺ babies attacked. Prevention: RhoGAM.
Common passage for air and food
Pharynx: shared by respiratory (air) and digestive (food) systems. Epiglottis covers glottis during swallowing → prevents food entering trachea.
Seminiferous tubules: site of sperm production (~1000/second). ~500-1000 per testis. Sertoli cells nourish developing sperm. Leydig cells between tubules.
Vitamin K: cofactor for synthesis of clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X, proteins C & S). Deficiency: bleeding. Warfarin inhibits vitamin K (anticoagulant).
Lymph differs from blood in lacking:
Lymph: similar to plasma but lacks RBCs (no hemoglobin), has fewer proteins (large ones can't leak out). Drains interstitial fluid back to blood via thoracic duct.
Sphincter of Oddi: at ampulla of Vater (where bile duct + pancreatic duct meet). Regulates release of bile + pancreatic juice into duodenum.
Trypsinogen is activated by which enzyme?
Enterokinase (from small intestine mucosa) converts trypsinogen → trypsin. Trypsin then activates other proenzymes (chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase).
Insulin: β-cells of pancreas (islets of Langerhans). Lowers blood glucose (promotes uptake, glycogen synthesis). Diabetes: deficiency (Type 1) or resistance (Type 2).
Filariasis: Wuchereria bancrofti (nematode, transmitted by Culex mosquito). Lymphatic obstruction → elephantiasis (gross swelling of limbs, genitals).
Cnidaria: radial symmetry, tissue level, cnidocytes (stinging cells). Examples: Hydra, jellyfish, sea anemone, corals. Two body forms: polyp + medusa.
Dental formula of adult human is:
Adult: I 2/2, C 1/1, PM 2/2, M 3/3 per quadrant = 32 teeth. Dental formula 2123/2123 represents 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, 3 molars per side per jaw.
Bile is produced by which organ?
Bile produced by liver, stored + concentrated in gallbladder. Contains bile salts (emulsify fat) and bile pigments (bilirubin). Released into duodenum via bile duct.
Platyhelminthes (flatworms): dorsoventrally flat, bilateral, triploblastic, acoelomate. Free-living (planaria) or parasitic (tapeworm, liver fluke).
Large intestine (colon): absorbs water, electrolytes from undigested material. Forms + stores feces. Bacteria produce vitamin K, biotin.
Penicillin: Fleming (1928) from Penicillium notatum mold. Mass production: Florey + Chain (WWII). First antibiotic. Started antibiotic era.
Arthropoda: ~80% of animal species. Jointed legs, exoskeleton (chitin), segmented body. Insects, spiders, crustaceans, centipedes, millipedes.
Blue baby: cyanosis (skin bluish) due to inadequate oxygenation. Causes: congenital heart defects (tetralogy of Fallot, transposition of great vessels).
RMP: ~−70 mV (inside negative). Due to K⁺ leak channels + Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase (3Na⁺ out, 2K⁺ in). Maintained by selective permeability.
Loop of Henle is located in:
Loop of Henle: extends from cortex (PCT) into medulla and back. Creates concentration gradient (countercurrent multiplier). Longer in desert animals.
Reflex: rapid, involuntary response to stimulus. Path: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector. Brain informed later.
Brunner's glands: submucosal glands in duodenum. Secrete alkaline mucus (bicarbonate-rich) to neutralize stomach acid + protect duodenal mucosa.
Carbonic anhydrase enzyme is present in:
Carbonic anhydrase in RBCs catalyzes: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ → HCO₃⁻ + H⁺. Enables efficient CO₂ transport. Zinc-containing enzyme.
Plasmid: small circular extra-chromosomal DNA in bacteria. Carries accessory genes (antibiotic resistance). Used as vectors in genetic engineering.
Appendix: vestigial (remnant of cecum for cellulose digestion in herbivores). Contains lymphoid tissue (minor immune function). Appendicitis: inflammation.
Phases of menstrual cycle in order:
Day 1: start of menstruation (uterine lining sheds). Follicular: FSH → follicle grows, estrogen. Ovulation (~day 14): LH surge. Luteal: corpus luteum, progesterone.
LH surge (day 14): triggers ovulation (follicle rupture, egg release). High estrogen → positive feedback to pituitary → LH surge.
Amphibia: dual life (aquatic larva, terrestrial adult). Moist skin (cutaneous respiration). 3-chambered heart. External fertilization. Need water for reproduction.
RBC lifespan: ~120 days. Removed by spleen ('graveyard of RBCs') and liver. Iron recycled (transferrin), heme → bilirubin (bile pigment).
C-shaped cartilage rings: keep trachea open. Posterior gap (smooth muscle) allows esophagus to expand during swallowing.
Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid): adrenal cortex. 'Salt-retaining hormone'. ↑Na⁺ reabsorption in kidney → water follows → ↑blood volume. RAAS system.
Number of bones in human hand:
Each hand: 27 bones. Carpals 8, metacarpals 5, phalanges 14 (2 in thumb, 3 in each other finger). Allows dexterity.
Proteins → amino acids by proteases (pepsin, trypsin, chymotrypsin, peptidases). Absorbed by active transport in small intestine.
GFR: ~125 mL/min × 1440 min = 180,000 mL = 180 L/day. 99% reabsorbed → ~1.5 L urine/day. Decreased GFR indicates kidney disease.
Fight or flight response is by:
Sympathetic: stress (fight/flight). ↑HR, ↑BP, dilates pupils, ↑blood sugar, ↓digestion. Uses norepinephrine. Parasympathetic: rest/digest (acetylcholine).
Urea is formed in which organ?
Urea cycle (Krebs-Henseleit, liver): converts toxic ammonia (from protein breakdown) to urea (less toxic). 2 NH₃ + CO₂ → urea + H₂O. Excreted by kidneys.
Placenta: maternal (decidua basalis) + fetal (chorionic villi). Provides nutrition, gas exchange, waste removal, hormones (HCG, progesterone, estrogen).
Calcitonin: thyroid C cells (parafollicular). Lowers blood calcium (deposits in bone). Antagonistic to PTH (parathyroid hormone). Minor role in humans.
Jenner (1796): inoculated boy with cowpox (milder) → immunity to smallpox. 'Vaccination' from 'vacca' (cow). Smallpox eradicated (1980, WHO).
Olfactory: upper nasal cavity. ~10 million receptors. Direct connection to limbic system (smell triggers memory). Anosmia: loss of smell (COVID symptom).
Average blood volume in adult human:
Blood volume: ~5-6 L in adults (7-8% of body weight). Plasma (55%) + cells (45%). RBCs ~5 million/mm³, WBCs ~7000/mm³, platelets ~250,000/mm³.
FSH: anterior pituitary. Females: stimulates follicle development in ovaries. Males: spermatogenesis. Gonadotropin (acts on gonads).
TB: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Koch, 1882). Affects lungs (pulmonary). Spread by droplets (cough). Symptoms: persistent cough, blood, weight loss. DOTS treatment.
Saltatory: AP 'jumps' between nodes of Ranvier (gaps in myelin). Faster (up to 120 m/s) + energy efficient. Unmyelinated: continuous, slower (~1 m/s).
Number of ova at birth in female:
