Females born with ~1-2 million oocytes. Puberty: ~300,000-400,000. Only ~400 ovulated in reproductive years. Stops at menopause (~45-55 years).
Thyroxine (T₄): thyroid gland. Needs iodine. Increases metabolic rate, growth, development. Deficiency: goiter, cretinism (children), myxedema (adults).
Knee: hinge joint (flexion/extension). Largest joint. Contains menisci (cartilage). Allows 1-axis movement (front-back). Patella protects.
Number of deciduous (milk) teeth in child:
Deciduous teeth: 20. I 2/2, C 1/1, M 2/2 per quadrant. Appear 6 months - 2.5 years. Replaced by permanent teeth from age 6.
Peristalsis: involuntary wave-like smooth muscle contractions. Moves food through GI tract. Controlled by enteric nervous system + hormones.
RV: air remaining after max expiration (~1200 mL). Prevents lung collapse (atelectasis). Cannot be exhaled. Keeps alveoli inflated.
Number of types of cones (color vision):
3 types of cones: S (blue, 420 nm), M (green, 530 nm), L (red, 560 nm). Trichromatic vision. Color blindness: missing/mutated cone type (often red-green).
Implantation: uterine wall (endometrium). ~7 days after fertilization. Blastocyst embeds. Endometrium thickens under progesterone to receive embryo.
Symbiosis (mutualism): both benefit. Lichen: fungus (structure, water) + algae (food, photosynthesis). Mycorrhiza, Rhizobium also mutualistic.
Cerebellum: 'little brain'. Coordinates voluntary movement, balance, posture. Alcohol affects it (drunkenness). Damage → ataxia (uncoordinated movement).
Two species can't occupy same niche indefinitely
Gause (1934): two species with identical niche → one extinct (outcompeted). Resource partitioning allows coexistence (slight niche differences).
Lacteal: lymph capillary in center of each villus. Absorbs dietary fats (chylomicrons). Fat → lymph → bloodstream via thoracic duct.
BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin): attenuated M. bovis. Given at birth in India. Variable efficacy (50-80%) vs pulmonary TB, better vs severe childhood TB.
PTH: parathyroid (4 small glands behind thyroid). Raises blood Ca²⁺: bone resorption (osteoclasts), kidney reabsorption, activates vitamin D → gut absorption.
Oxygen is transported in blood mainly as:
O₂ transport: 98.5% as HbO₂ (oxyhemoglobin), 1.5% dissolved in plasma. CO₂ transport: 70% as HCO₃⁻, 23% as carbamino-Hb, 7% dissolved.
Jenner (1796): inoculated boy with cowpox (milder) → immunity to smallpox. 'Vaccination' from 'vacca' (cow). Smallpox eradicated (1980, WHO).
ABO blood groups were discovered by:
Landsteiner (1900): ABO blood groups. Later (with Wiener, 1937-40): Rh factor. Nobel Prize 1930. Made safe blood transfusions possible.
Subphylum of chordates with vertebral column:
Vertebrata: notochord replaced by vertebral column in adults. Largest chordate subphylum. Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals. ~57,000 species.
Progesterone: corpus luteum (after ovulation). Maintains endometrium for pregnancy. Placenta takes over in pregnancy. 'Pregnancy hormone'. Birth control pills contain progesterone.
Hemichordata: 'half chordate'. Worm-like marine animals. Body: proboscis, collar, trunk. Believed to be link between echinoderms and chordates.
Restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) cut DNA at:
Restriction enzymes (endonucleases): cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences (e.g., EcoRI: GAATTC). 'Molecular scissors'. Found in bacteria (defense vs phages).
Class of fishes with cartilaginous skeleton:
Chondrichthyes: cartilaginous fish (sharks, rays, skates). Predators. Placoid scales. No operculum. 5-7 gill slits. Spiral valve intestine.
Class of fishes with bony skeleton:
Osteichthyes: bony fish (largest vertebrate class, ~25,000 species). Operculum covers gills. Swim bladder (buoyancy). Examples: rohu, tuna, salmon.
Hep B: HBV virus. Affects liver. Transmitted: blood, sex, mother-to-child. Vaccine available (first anti-cancer vaccine, prevents liver cancer).
FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone): anterior pituitary. Females: follicle development. Males: spermatogenesis (Sertoli cells). Gonadotropin.
Medulla: vital centers - respiratory, cardiac, vasomotor (BP). Also reflexes: vomiting, coughing, sneezing, swallowing. Damage → death.
Iris: colored part (pigment). Controls pupil size (light regulation). Brown: most common. Blue: less melanin. Albino: no pigment (red/pink).
Mutualism: both benefit. Bees get nectar, flowers get pollinated. Lichens, mycorrhiza, Rhizobium-legume. Common in nature, evolved co-dependence.
Ovulation in human females is triggered by:
LH surge (mid-cycle, day 14): triggers ovulation (follicle rupture, egg release). High estrogen → positive feedback to pituitary → LH surge.
Number of teeth in adult human:
Adult: 32 teeth (16 each jaw). 4 incisors, 2 canines, 4 premolars, 6 molars per jaw. Wisdom teeth (3rd molars) often impacted.
Hypothalamus: homeostasis (temp, hunger, thirst, sleep, circadian rhythm). Controls pituitary (master gland). Links nervous + endocrine systems.
Enzyme in stomach that digests proteins:
Pepsin: secreted as pepsinogen (inactive) by chief cells. HCl (parietal cells) activates → pepsin. Digests proteins → peptides. pH ~2.
Carbohydrates → monosaccharides. Starch → maltose (amylase) → glucose (maltase). Sucrose → glucose + fructose. Lactose → glucose + galactose.
Sperm survival in female reproductive tract:
Sperm: viable ~48-72 hours in female tract. Egg: viable ~12-24 hours. Fertile window: ~5 days before ovulation + day of ovulation.
Flap that covers glottis during swallowing
Epiglottis: elastic cartilage flap. During swallowing, closes glottis (opening to larynx) → food goes to esophagus, not lungs. Prevents choking.
Birds/reptiles: uricotelic (uric acid). Semi-solid, conserves water (needed for flight + egg-laying). White paste in bird droppings.
Sutures: immovable fibrous joints between skull bones. Allow growth in childhood, fuse in adult. Fontanelles: soft spots in infants.
Tidal volume: ~500 mL. Air moved in normal quiet breathing. Inspiratory reserve (IRV): ~3000 mL. Expiratory reserve (ERV): ~1100 mL.
Hemoglobin is present in which cells?
Hemoglobin in RBCs (~280 million per RBC). Carries O₂ (oxyhemoglobin) and some CO₂ (carbamino-Hb). Gives blood red color.
Gene therapy was first used for:
1990: Ashanti DeSilva (4 yrs), ADA deficiency (severe combined immunodeficiency - 'bubble boy'). WBCs modified with normal ADA gene. Limited success.
Menopause: cessation of menstruation (12 months no period). Avg age 51. Symptoms: hot flashes, mood changes, osteoporosis risk. Due to estrogen decline, follicle depletion.
Innate (non-specific): skin, mucus, phagocytes, complement, inflammation. First line, no memory. Acquired (adaptive): specific, has memory (B/T cells).
Number of nephrons in each kidney:
Each kidney: ~1 million nephrons. Cannot regenerate. Total ~2 million. Filtration rate: ~125 mL/min → 180 L/day filtrate (99% reabsorbed → 1.5 L urine).
O-negative: no A, B antigens (no rejection), no Rh (no Rh incompatibility). Universal donor. AB-positive: universal recipient (has all antigens).
LH: anterior pituitary. Females: triggers ovulation, maintains corpus luteum (progesterone). Males: stimulates testosterone (Leydig cells).
Salivary amylase acts in which part of digestive system?
Salivary amylase (ptyalin) acts in mouth (pH 6.8) breaking starch → maltose. Inactivated by stomach acid. Pancreatic amylase continues in small intestine.
Annelida: segmented worms. Earthworm (Pheretima), leech (Hirudinaria). Metameric segmentation, closed circulation, true coelom.
Two species competing for same food
Competition: organisms compete for same resource. Intraspecific (same species) more intense. Inter-specific (different species). Gause's competitive exclusion.
Antibodies (immunoglobulins, Ig): produced by plasma cells (mature B cells). 5 classes: IgG (most common), IgM (first responder), IgA (mucosa), IgE (allergy), IgD.
Arthropoda (jointed legs): largest animal phylum. Exoskeleton (chitin), segmented body. Insects, crustaceans, arachnids.
Cones are of how many types (color vision):
3 types of cones: S (blue, 420 nm), M (green, 530 nm), L (red, 560 nm). Trichromatic vision. Color blindness: missing/mutated cone type (often red-green).
Adrenaline: adrenal medulla. 'Fight or flight'. ↑HR, ↑BP, ↑blood sugar, dilates airways, dilates pupils. Stress hormone. Also neurotransmitter.
Bile: produced by liver, stored in gallbladder. Contains bile salts (emulsify fat), bile pigments (bilirubin). No digestive enzymes.
Estrogen: growing follicle in ovary. Female secondary sexual characteristics (breasts, hips), endometrial proliferation. Birth control pills contain estrogen.
Number of heart chambers in human:
Human heart: 4 chambers. Right atrium + ventricle (deoxygenated blood), left atrium + ventricle (oxygenated blood). Septum separates.
Bile and pancreatic juice entry to duodenum
Sphincter of Oddi: at ampulla of Vater (where bile duct + pancreatic duct meet). Controls release of bile + pancreatic juice into duodenum.
Most synapses chemical: presynaptic releases neurotransmitter → binds postsynaptic receptors. Some electrical (gap junctions, cardiac muscle, retina).
Villi: finger-like projections in small intestine. Each villus: epithelium, lacteal (lymph capillary), blood capillaries. Increase absorption area.
Aedes aegypti: vector for dengue, yellow fever, Zika, chikungunya. Day-biting. Breeds in clean stagnant water. Tiger-striped legs.
Porifera: sponges. Simplest animals. Cellular level (no true tissues). Pore-bearing body. Filter feeders. Mostly marine.
Mammalia: mammary glands (milk), hair/fur, 3 middle ear bones, diaphragm, 4-chambered heart, warm-blooded. Mostly viviparous (except monotremes - egg-laying).
Gene therapy was first successfully used for:
1990: Ashanti DeSilva (4 yrs), ADA deficiency (severe combined immunodeficiency, 'bubble boy'). WBCs modified with normal ADA gene. Limited success.
Deoxygenated blood from heart to lungs
Unique: pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood (heart → lungs for oxygenation). Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood (lungs → heart). Exception to normal pattern.
Aldosterone (adrenal cortex): 'salt-retaining hormone'. Acts on DCT + collecting duct. Na⁺ reabsorbed → water follows → ↑ blood volume + pressure.
Sympathetic: stress (fight/flight). ↑HR, ↑BP, dilates pupils, ↑blood sugar, ↓digestion. Uses norepinephrine. Parasympathetic: rest/digest (acetylcholine).
Predation: predator kills/eats prey. Lion-deer, snake-mouse, eagle-rabbit. Drives evolution (predator-prey arms race). Maintains population balance.
Adult (permanent): I 2/2, C 1/1, PM 2/2, M 3/3 per quadrant = 32 teeth. Dental formula: 2123/2123 = 2I+1C+2PM+3M on each side per jaw.
Femur: longest, strongest bone. ~45 cm in adult. Upper leg. Head fits into acetabulum (hip socket). Carries body weight.
Oxygen transported in blood mainly as:
O₂ transport: 98.5% as oxyhemoglobin (HbO₂). ~1.5% dissolved in plasma. CO₂ transport: 70% bicarbonate, 23% carbamino, 7% dissolved.
Fish: ammonotelic (ammonia). Very toxic, needs lots of water. Aquatic environment dilutes it. Removed via gills.
Trypsin: pancreatic protease. Secreted as trypsinogen (inactive). Activated by enterokinase (small intestine). Digests proteins → peptides.
SA node: right atrium wall. Generates electrical impulses (~70-80/min). Sets rhythm. Called natural pacemaker. Influenced by autonomic nervous system.
Bt cotton: contains gene from Bacillus thuringiensis. Produces Bt toxin (Cry protein) → kills bollworm. Specific to insects (safe for humans). Reduces pesticide use.
Double circulation: pulmonary (heart → lungs → heart) + systemic (heart → body → heart). Separates oxygenated/deoxygenated. Efficient.
Parasitism: parasite benefits, host harmed. Tapeworm in intestine absorbs nutrients. Mosquito (ectoparasite) on human. Cuscuta (plant parasite).
Malaria: Plasmodium (falciparum, vivax, malariae, ovale). Vector: female Anopheles mosquito. Affects RBCs → fever, chills, anemia.
Melatonin: pineal gland (brain). Regulates circadian rhythm (sleep-wake cycle). Released in dark. Light inhibits. Jet lag, shift work disrupt.
Insulin produced by genetic engineering uses:
Recombinant insulin (1982, first product of biotech): human insulin gene inserted in E. coli. Produces insulin identical to human. Replaced animal insulin (allergies).
Knee-jerk: monosynaptic (only 2 neurons: sensory + motor, no interneuron). Stretch of quadriceps tendon → tap of patellar ligament → leg extension.
Number of bones in middle ear:
Middle ear ossicles: malleus (hammer), incus (anvil), stapes (stirrup). Smallest bones. Transmit vibrations from eardrum to inner ear (oval window).
Aorta: largest artery. Origin: left ventricle. Distributes oxygenated blood to body. Diameter ~2.5 cm. Walls thick to withstand pressure.
Aorta: largest artery. Origin: left ventricle. Distributes oxygenated blood to body. Diameter ~2.5 cm. Walls thick (withstand high pressure).
After fertilization: zygote (1 cell) → morula (16 cells, solid ball) → blastocyst (hollow ball with inner cell mass) → implants → embryo → fetus (after 8 weeks).
RBC lifespan: ~120 days. Destroyed in spleen (graveyard of RBCs) and liver. Iron recycled (transferrin), heme → bilirubin (bile pigment).
Shoulder (glenohumeral): ball and socket. Most mobile joint → most prone to dislocation. Allows flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, rotation, circumduction.
Cholera: Vibrio cholerae. Spread by contaminated water/food. Causes severe diarrhea, dehydration. ORS (oral rehydration) treatment saves lives.
Glomerulus: tuft of capillaries inside Bowman's capsule. Site of filtration. Blood pressure forces fluid + small molecules out → filtrate.
Number of spinal nerves in humans:
Spinal nerves: 31 pairs. Cervical 8, Thoracic 12, Lumbar 5, Sacral 5, Coccygeal 1. All mixed (sensory + motor). Form plexuses (networks).
Recombinant DNA: combine DNA from different organisms. Tools: restriction enzymes, ligases, vectors (plasmids), host (E. coli). Used for insulin, vaccines, GM crops.
Lub: AV valves (mitral, tricuspid) close. Dub: semilunar valves (aortic, pulmonary) close. Heard with stethoscope. Abnormal: murmurs (regurgitation).
Normal: 120/80 mmHg. Systolic (ventricular contraction) / Diastolic (relaxation). Hypertension: >140/90. Hypotension: <90/60.
ADH (vasopressin): from posterior pituitary. Makes collecting duct permeable to water → water reabsorbed → concentrated urine. Alcohol inhibits ADH (diuretic).
Porifera (pore-bearers): sponges. Simplest animals. No true tissues (cellular level). Filter feeders. Mostly marine. Body full of pores (ostia).
Seminiferous tubules: site of sperm production. ~500-1000 per testis. Sertoli cells nourish developing sperm. Leydig cells (between tubules) make testosterone.
hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is secreted by:
hCG: placenta (after implantation). Maintains corpus luteum → progesterone → maintains pregnancy. Detected in pregnancy tests (urine, blood).
Mollusca (soft body): mantle (shell-secreting), muscular foot, radula (rasping tongue). Examples: snail, octopus, squid, oyster. Mostly marine, some freshwater.
Enterokinase (small intestinal mucosa): converts trypsinogen → trypsin. Trypsin then activates more trypsinogen + other proenzymes (chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase).
Golden rice is engineered to produce:
Golden rice: engineered to produce β-carotene (precursor of vitamin A) in endosperm. Fights vitamin A deficiency (blindness). Created by Potrykus + Beyer.
Spermatogenesis starts at puberty (~12-14 years). Continues throughout life (decreases with age). ~1000 sperm/second. Cycle: ~64-74 days.
Hemoglobin: 4 polypeptide chains (2α + 2β) + 4 heme groups (each with Fe²⁺). Each Fe binds 1 O₂. ~280 million Hb per RBC. ~1 billion O₂ per RBC.
Cerebrum: ~85% brain mass. Two hemispheres. Outer cortex (grey matter, ~2-4 mm thick). Higher functions: thought, memory, voluntary movement, language.
Vagus (10th cranial): longest. Mixed nerve. Supplies heart, lungs, stomach, intestines. Main parasympathetic nerve. Controls HR, digestion.
Endosperm: 3n (from triple fusion: 1 sperm + 2 polar nuclei). Nutritive tissue for embryo. In cereals persists (food). In beans consumed by cotyledons.
Logistic: dN/dt = rN(1 - N/K). Sigmoid. Phases: lag, exponential, deceleration, stable (at K). Realistic for most populations in nature.
Myxedema: adult hypothyroidism. Symptoms: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, mental sluggishness. Treatment: thyroxine replacement.
Restriction endonucleases: cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences (e.g., EcoRI: GAATTC). 'Molecular scissors'. Found in bacteria (defense vs phages).
Exchange of gases between alveoli and blood:
External respiration: alveoli ↔ blood. Internal respiration: blood ↔ tissues. Cellular respiration: in cells (mitochondria, produces ATP).
Adrenaline (epinephrine): adrenal medulla. 'Fight or flight'. ↑HR, ↑BP, ↑blood sugar, dilates airways. Stress hormone. Also a neurotransmitter.
Cretinism: childhood hypothyroidism. Symptoms: stunted growth, mental retardation, low body temp, coarse facial features. Preventable with early screening + treatment.
Pupil: black circular opening in iris. Allows light to enter eye. Size controlled by iris muscles (constricts in bright light, dilates in dark).
Pulmonary: heart → lungs → heart (deoxygenated blood to lungs, oxygenated back). Systemic: heart → body → heart. Double circulation in mammals.
Vital capacity: max air exhaled after max inhalation. IRV (3000 mL) + TV (500 mL) + ERV (1100 mL) = 4600 mL. Reduced in lung diseases.
Number of chambers in human heart:
Human heart: 4 chambers (2 atria + 2 ventricles). Right: deoxygenated blood. Left: oxygenated. Septum separates. Prevents mixing (efficient).
Corpus luteum: from ruptured follicle after ovulation. Secretes progesterone (maintains endometrium) + some estrogen. If no pregnancy: regresses → menstruation. If pregnant: maintained by hCG.
Humans are ureotelic (urea). Fish: ammonotelic (ammonia, very soluble, needs water). Birds/reptiles: uricotelic (uric acid, semi-solid, water conservation).
C-shaped cartilage rings keep trachea open. Gap at back (smooth muscle) allows esophagus to expand during swallowing of food.
Sperm count per ejaculation in healthy male:
Normal: 200-500 million per ejaculation (~2-5 mL). <20 million/mL = low count (oligospermia). Most don't reach egg. Only ~200 reach ampulla. 1 fertilizes.
Larynx: vocal cords (2 pairs). Air passes → cords vibrate → sound. Pitch depends on cord tension. Located between pharynx and trachea.
Thickest wall of heart is in:
Left ventricle: thickest wall (pumps blood to entire body via aorta, high pressure needed). Right ventricle: thinner (only pumps to lungs).
Brain stem: midbrain + pons + medulla oblongata. Connects brain to spinal cord. Vital functions: breathing, HR, BP, consciousness, sleep.
Pepsin: secreted as pepsinogen (inactive) by chief cells. HCl (parietal cells) activates → pepsin. Digests proteins → peptides. pH ~2.
CO₂ transported in blood mainly as:
CO₂ transport: 70% as HCO₃⁻ (in RBC via carbonic anhydrase), 23% as carbamino-Hb, 7% dissolved. Reverse in lungs → exhaled.
Rods (~120 million): dim light, B/W. Cones (~6 million): color, bright light. Fovea centralis (in macula): only cones, sharpest vision.
Neuron (nerve cell): structural + functional unit. ~86 billion in brain. Parts: dendrites (input), cell body (soma), axon (output). Synapse: junction.
Inner ear cochlea is responsible for:
Cochlea: snail-shaped, contains organ of Corti (hair cells). Sound → vibrations → fluid waves → hair cells bend → nerve impulses → brain.
GH (somatotropin): anterior pituitary. Stimulates growth, cell reproduction. Hyper: gigantism (children), acromegaly (adults). Hypo: dwarfism (children).
Amniotic fluid: cushion (protects from mechanical shock), maintains temperature, allows movement (muscle development), prevents adhesions. ~800 mL at term.
Two species can't occupy same niche indefinitely
Gause (1934): two species with identical niche → one extinct (outcompeted). Resource partitioning allows coexistence (slight niche differences).
Length of small intestine in humans:
Small intestine: ~6 m. Duodenum (25 cm), jejunum (2.5 m), ileum (3.5 m). Adaptation for absorption (large surface area: villi + microvilli).
Respiratory center: medulla (rhythm generation) + pons (regulation). Responds to CO₂ via chemoreceptors (aorta, carotid arteries).
SA node (sinoatrial): right atrium wall. Generates electrical impulses ~70-80/min. Sets heart rhythm. Natural pacemaker.
Echinodermata (spiny skin): radial symmetry (adults, bilateral larvae), water vascular system, tube feet. Marine. Examples: starfish, sea urchin, sea cucumber.
Taq polymerase used in PCR is isolated from:
Taq polymerase: from Thermus aquaticus (Yellowstone hot springs). Thermostable (survives 95°C). Critical for PCR (no need to add fresh enzyme each cycle).
Golden rice is genetically modified to produce:
Golden rice: engineered to produce β-carotene (precursor of vitamin A) in endosperm. Fights vitamin A deficiency (blindness). Created by Ingo Potrykus + Peter Beyer.
Glucagon: α-cells of pancreas. Raises blood glucose (glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis). Antagonistic to insulin. Maintains blood sugar in fasting.
Taq polymerase: from Thermus aquaticus (thermophilic bacterium from Yellowstone hot springs). Thermostable (survives 95°C). Critical for PCR automation.
Notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail
Chordata: 4 key features (at some life stage): notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, post-anal tail. Vertebrates are subphylum.
Testosterone: Leydig (interstitial) cells of testes. Male secondary sexual characteristics, spermatogenesis, muscle/bone mass. Anabolic steroid.
Cerebrum: largest (~85% brain mass). Two hemispheres. Outer cortex (grey matter). Higher functions: thought, memory, voluntary movement.
Most digestion and absorption occurs in:
Small intestine: ~6m long (duodenum, jejunum, ileum). Villi + microvilli increase surface area (~250 m²). Most nutrients absorbed here.
Exchange of gases between alveoli and blood is called:
External respiration: alveoli ↔ blood (O₂ in, CO₂ out). Internal: blood ↔ tissues. Cellular: in cells (mitochondria, produces ATP).
Thyroxine (T₄): 4 iodine atoms. T₃: 3 iodine. Deficiency of iodine → goiter (enlarged thyroid), cretinism (children). Prevented by iodized salt.
Pepsin is secreted by which cells of stomach?
Pepsinogen (inactive) secreted by chief cells. Activated to pepsin by HCl (from parietal cells). Digests proteins to peptides in stomach at pH ~2.
Antibiotics: kill/inhibit bacteria. Targets: cell wall (penicillin), protein synthesis (tetracycline). NO effect on viruses (use antivirals). Misuse → resistance.
Threshold: ~-55 mV (depolarization). Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open → Na⁺ influx → depolarization to +30 mV (peak). Then K⁺ efflux → repolarization.
Exponential (geometric): dN/dt = rN. J-shaped. Possible when resources unlimited (rare, short-term). Bacterial growth, invasive species initially.
Cerebellum: 'little brain'. Coordinates voluntary movement, balance, posture. Damage → ataxia (loss of coordination). Alcohol affects cerebellum (drunkenness).
Cortisol (glucocorticoid): adrenal cortex. Stress hormone. ↑Blood sugar (gluconeogenesis), anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive. Synthetic: prednisone, dexamethasone.
Proteins → amino acids. Pepsin, trypsin, chymotrypsin → peptides. Peptidases → amino acids. Absorbed by active transport.
Fertilization: ampulla (widest part of fallopian tube). Sperm meets egg ~12-24 hours after ovulation. Zygote → morula → blastocyst → implants in uterus (~7 days).
Arthropoda (jointed legs): largest phylum (~80% animal species). Exoskeleton (chitin), segmented body, jointed appendages. Insects, crustaceans, arachnids.
Knee: hinge joint (flexion/extension only). Largest joint. Has menisci (cartilage), cruciate ligaments. Allows 1-axis movement (front-back).
Aschelminthes (Nematoda, roundworms): cylindrical, bilateral, pseudocoelomate. Examples: Ascaris (human intestine), Wuchereria (filariasis).
Rhodopsin: opsin + retinal (vitamin A derivative). Light → retinal isomerizes → signal. Vitamin A deficiency → night blindness.
Where optic nerve exits retina (no photoreceptors)
Blind spot: optic disc (where optic nerve exits). No photoreceptors. Brain 'fills in' the missing area. Testable with visual field test.
Rugae: longitudinal folds in stomach wall. Allow expansion when food enters. Also in palate (palatal rugae).
Lacteal is found in which structure?
Lacteal: lymph capillary in center of each intestinal villus. Absorbs dietary fats (as chylomicrons) → lymph → bloodstream via thoracic duct.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used to:
PCR (Mullis, 1983, Nobel 1993): amplifies DNA in vitro. Cycles: denaturation (95°C), annealing (50-65°C), extension (72°C, Taq polymerase). Millions of copies in hours.
Number of bones in adult human:
Adult: 206 bones. Newborn: ~270-300 (some fuse). Spine: 33 (some fused). Hand: 27 each. Axial skeleton: 80. Appendicular: 126.
Sperm can survive in female tract for:
Sperm viable ~48-72 hrs in female reproductive tract. Egg viable ~12-24 hrs. Fertile window: ~5 days before ovulation + day of ovulation.
Vestibular: 3 semicircular canals (X, Y, Z axes) + utricle + saccule. Detect head position + movement. Fluid (endolymph) moves → hair cells detect.
